note.has-max: the specificity of :has() is that of the most specific selector in its argument list.
note.nth-of: an :nth-child() or :nth-last-child() with an of clause counts as one pseudo-class plus the most specific selector after of.
note.legacy-pseudo-element: a single-colon pseudo-element from CSS2 (:before, :after, :first-line, :first-letter): still a pseudo-element, counted in C.
note.host-plus: :host() and :host-context() count as one pseudo-class plus their argument (CSS Shadow Module Level 1).
note.slotted-plus: ::slotted() counts as one pseudo-element plus its argument (CSS Shadow Module Level 1).
note.part: ::part() is counted as one pseudo-element; the Shadow module defers its exact specificity to CSS Pseudo-Elements Level 4.
note.repeated: a repeat of a simple selector already in this compound: repeated occurrences are allowed and do increase specificity.

error.unbalanced: An opening bracket or parenthesis at position {at} is never closed.
error.dangling-combinator: A combinator at position {at} with nothing on one side of it.
error.unexpected: A character at position {at} that cannot start a simple selector (a declaration pasted as a selector, or a typo).

css-specificity-calculator.cascadeTitle: What the cascade checks before specificity
css-specificity-calculator.cascadeIntro: Specificity decides only when everything above it is equal. CSS Cascading and Inheritance Level 5 sorts declarations by these criteria, in descending order of priority:

cascade.origin: Origin and importance: transitions first, then important user-agent, important user, important author, animations, normal author, normal user, normal user-agent declarations. An !important author declaration beats every normal one regardless of selector.
cascade.context: Context: between shadow-tree contexts, the outer context wins for normal declarations and the inner one for important declarations.
cascade.attached: Element-attached styles: a style attribute beats any style rule of the same importance.
cascade.layers: Cascade layers: for normal declarations the last layer wins, for important ones the first; declarations outside any layer sit in an implicit final layer.
cascade.specificity: Specificity: the triple compared here. Each declaration has the specificity of its rule's selector.
cascade.order: Order of appearance: the last declaration in document order wins, with style attributes placed after every style sheet.

css-specificity-calculator.limits: The calculator reads selector syntax, not a document: it cannot know whether a selector matches anything, and a selector list is ranked by its own members, while in a real match the specificity in effect is that of the most specific member that matches. Namespaces are read but not resolved. The counting follows Selectors Level 4 (Working Draft, 22 January 2026) and the cascade order follows CSS Cascade Level 5; both are cited under Sources.

share.carries: The link carries the selectors as typed, and nothing else.

err.tooLong: The input is longer than {max} characters.

html-structure-explainer.name: HTML structure & DOM explainer
html-structure-explainer.blurb: Paste HTML and read the tree the HTML parser builds from it: every element, text node and comment with its line, the elements the parser created without a tag (html, head, body, tbody), the end tags it supplied, the formatting elements it split and the content it moved out of a table, with the document mode (quirks or not) and every parse error by the standard's own code and position. Then the findings: the DOCTYPE, the language, the title, the encoding, images without alternative text, links and buttons with no name, heading jumps, duplicate ids, controls without labels, obsolete elements and attributes, each tied to a sentence of the HTML Standard or WCAG 2.2. Parsing only: no script runs, nothing is fetched, nothing is rendered.
html-structure-explainer.htmlLabel: HTML (a whole document or a fragment)
html-structure-explainer.summary: {elements, plural, one {One element} other {# elements}}, {texts, plural, one {one text node} other {# text nodes}} and {comments, plural, =0 {no comments} one {one comment} other {# comments}}, {depth, plural, one {one level} other {# levels}} deep, from {lines, plural, one {one line} other {# lines}} of source.
html-structure-explainer.errorsSummary: {n, plural, =0 {No parse errors.} one {One parse error.} other {# parse errors.}}
html-structure-explainer.findingsSummary: Findings: {errors, plural, =0 {no errors} one {one error} other {# errors}}, {warnings, plural, =0 {no warnings} one {one warning} other {# warnings}}, {notes, plural, =0 {no notes} one {one note} other {# notes}}.

modeNote.no-quirks: The standards mode: <!DOCTYPE html> or an equivalent was found first.
modeNote.limited-quirks: A legacy DOCTYPE with a system identifier: almost standards mode, with a few table-cell and inline-image quirks kept.
modeNote.quirks: The compatibility mode the parser falls into without a DOCTYPE or with an old one: the standard notes it is "incompatible with some specifications".

html-structure-explainer.treeIntro: Each row is one node, indented by depth, with the line of its tag in the source. {implied, plural, =0 {No element was created by the parser without a tag} one {One element was created by the parser without a tag} other {# elements were created by the parser without a tag}}, {omitted, plural, =0 {no end tag was supplied by the parser} one {one end tag was supplied by the parser} other {# end tags were supplied by the parser}}, {pieces, plural, =0 {no element was split} one {one element was split} other {# elements were split}}, {fostered, plural, =0 {nothing was moved out of a table} one {one node was moved out of a table} other {# nodes were moved out of a table}}; {whitespace, plural, =0 {no whitespace-only text node is left out of the list} one {one whitespace-only text node is left out of the list} other {# whitespace-only text nodes are left out of the list}}.
html-structure-explainer.treeTruncated: The list stops at {n} nodes; the counts above cover the whole tree.
html-structure-explainer.treeLegend: A dot in the line gutter marks a node with no source position: the parser created it. The pills say what the parser did: created (no tag in the source), end supplied (no end tag in the source), void (never has an end tag), self-closing (foreign content written with />), piece n (one source element split into several), moved (foster-parented before a table), obsolete (section 16.2 of the standard), template (lives in a template's content, not in the document).
html-structure-explainer.errorsTitle: {n, plural, =0 {Parse errors} one {One parse error} other {# parse errors}}
html-structure-explainer.noErrors: The parser raised no error: every tag, attribute, comment and character reference was well formed, and the tree is the one the markup asked for.

error.abrupt-closing-of-empty-comment: This error occurs if the parser encounters an empty comment that is abruptly closed by a U+003E (>) code point (i.e., <!--> or <!--->). The parser behaves as if the comment is closed correctly.
error.abrupt-doctype-public-identifier: This error occurs if the parser encounters a U+003E (>) code point in the DOCTYPE public identifier (e.g., <!DOCTYPE html PUBLIC "foo>). In such a case, if the DOCTYPE is correctly placed as a document preamble, the parser sets the Document to quirks mode.
error.abrupt-doctype-system-identifier: This error occurs if the parser encounters a U+003E (>) code point in the DOCTYPE system identifier (e.g., <!DOCTYPE html PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 4.01//EN" "foo>). In such a case, if the DOCTYPE is correctly placed as a document preamble, the parser sets the Document to quirks mode.
error.absence-of-digits-in-numeric-character-r: This error occurs if the parser encounters a numeric character reference that doesn't contain any digits (e.g., &#qux;). In this case the parser doesn't resolve the character reference.
error.cdata-in-html-content: This error occurs if the parser encounters a CDATA section outside of foreign content (SVG or MathML). The parser treats such CDATA sections (including leading "[CDATA[" and trailing "]]") as comments.
error.character-reference-outside-unicode-rang: This error occurs if the parser encounters a numeric character reference that references a code point that is greater than the valid Unicode range. The parser resolves such a character reference to a U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER.
error.control-character-in-input-stream: This error occurs if the input stream contains a control code point that is not ASCII whitespace or U+0000 NULL. Such code points are parsed as-is and usually, where parsing rules don't apply any additional restrictions, make their way into the DOM.
error.control-character-reference: This error occurs if the parser encounters a numeric character reference that references a control code point that is not ASCII whitespace or is a U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN. The parser resolves such character references as-is except C1 control references that are replaced according to the numeric character reference end state.
error.disallowed-processing-instruction-target: This error occurs if the parser encounters a processing instruction target that is an ASCII case-insensitive match for "xml" or "xml-stylesheet". The preceding U+003F (?) and all content that follows up to a U+003E (>) (if present) or to the end of the input stream is treated as a comment.
error.duplicate-attribute: This error occurs if the parser encounters an attribute in a tag that already has an attribute with the same name. The parser ignores all such duplicate occurrences of the attribute.
error.end-tag-with-attributes: This error occurs if the parser encounters an end tag with attributes. Attributes in end tags are ignored and do not make their way into the DOM.
error.end-tag-with-trailing-solidus: This error occurs if the parser encounters an end tag that has a U+002F (/) code point right before the closing U+003E (>) code point (e.g., '</div/>'). Such a tag is treated as a regular end tag.
error.eof-before-tag-name: This error occurs if the parser encounters the end of the input stream where a tag name is expected. In this case the parser treats the beginning of a start tag (i.e., '<') or an end tag (i.e., '</') as text content.
error.eof-in-cdata: This error occurs if the parser encounters the end of the input stream in a CDATA section. The parser treats such CDATA sections as if they are closed immediately before the end of the input stream.
error.eof-in-comment: This error occurs if the parser encounters the end of the input stream in a comment. The parser treats such comments as if they are closed immediately before the end of the input stream.
error.eof-in-doctype: This error occurs if the parser encounters the end of the input stream in a DOCTYPE. In such a case, if the DOCTYPE is correctly placed as a document preamble, the parser sets the Document to quirks mode.
error.eof-in-processing-instruction: This error occurs if the parser encounters the end of the input stream in a processing instruction (e.g., <? or <?marker name=). Such processing instructions are ignored.
error.eof-in-script-html-comment-like-text: This error occurs if the parser encounters the end of the input stream in text that resembles an HTML comment inside script element content (e.g., '<script>'<!-- foo). Syntactic structures that resemble HTML comments in script elements are parsed as text content. They can be a part of a scripting language-specific syntactic structure or be treated as an HTML-like comment, if the scripting language supports them (e.g., parsing rules for HTML-like comments can be found in Annex B of the JavaScript specification). The common reason for this error is a violation of the restrictions for contents of script elements.
error.eof-in-tag: This error occurs if the parser encounters the end of the input stream in a start tag or an end tag (e.g., '<div' id=). Such a tag is ignored.
error.incorrectly-closed-comment: This error occurs if the parser encounters a comment that is closed by the "--!>" code point sequence. The parser treats such comments as if they are correctly closed by the "-->" code point sequence.
error.incorrectly-opened-comment: This error occurs if the parser encounters the "<!" code point sequence that is not immediately followed by two U+002D (-) code points and that is not the start of a DOCTYPE or a CDATA section. All content that follows the "<!" code point sequence up to a U+003E (>) code point (if present) or to the end of the input stream is treated as a comment. One possible cause of this error is using an XML markup declaration (e.g., <!ELEMENT br EMPTY>) in HTML.
error.invalid-character-sequence-after-doctype: This error occurs if the parser encounters any code point sequence other than "PUBLIC" and "SYSTEM" keywords after a DOCTYPE name. In such a case, the parser ignores any following public or system identifiers, and if the DOCTYPE is correctly placed as a document preamble, and if the parser cannot change the mode flag is false, sets the Document to quirks mode.
error.invalid-first-character-of-processing-in: This error occurs if the parser encounters a code point that is not an ASCII alpha or U+005F (_) where the first code point of a processing instruction target is expected. The preceding U+003F (?) and all content that follows up to a U+003E (>) (if present) or to the end of the input stream is treated as a comment.
error.invalid-first-character-of-tag-name: This error occurs if the parser encounters a code point that is not an ASCII alpha where the first code point of a start tag name or an end tag name is expected. If a start tag was expected such code point and a preceding U+003C ('<') is treated as text content, and all content that follows is treated as markup. Whereas, if an end tag was expected, such code point and all content that follows up to a U+003E (>) code point (if present) or to the end of the input stream is treated as a comment.
error.invalid-processing-instruction-target: This error occurs if the parser encounters a code point that is not an ASCII alphanumeric, U+002D (-), or U+005F (_) where a processing instruction target is expected. The preceding U+003F (?) and all content that follows up to a U+003E (>) (if present) or to the end of the input stream is treated as a comment.
error.missing-attribute-value: This error occurs if the parser encounters a U+003E (>) code point where an attribute value is expected (e.g., '<div id=>'). The parser treats the attribute as having an empty value.
error.missing-doctype-name: This error occurs if the parser encounters a DOCTYPE that is missing a name (e.g., <!DOCTYPE>). In such a case, if the DOCTYPE is correctly placed as a document preamble, the parser sets the Document to quirks mode.
error.missing-doctype-public-identifier: This error occurs if the parser encounters a U+003E (>) code point where start of the DOCTYPE public identifier is expected (e.g., <!DOCTYPE html PUBLIC >). In such a case, if the DOCTYPE is correctly placed as a document preamble, the parser sets the Document to quirks mode.
error.missing-doctype-system-identifier: This error occurs if the parser encounters a U+003E (>) code point where start of the DOCTYPE system identifier is expected (e.g., <!DOCTYPE html SYSTEM >). In such a case, if the DOCTYPE is correctly placed as a document preamble, the parser sets the Document to quirks mode.
error.missing-end-tag-name: This error occurs if the parser encounters a U+003E (>) code point where an end tag name is expected, i.e., '</>'. The parser ignores the whole "'</>'" code point sequence.
error.missing-quote-before-doctype-public-iden: This error occurs if the parser encounters the DOCTYPE public identifier that is not preceded by a quote (e.g., <!DOCTYPE html PUBLIC -//W3C//DTD HTML 4.01//EN">). In such a case, the parser ignores the public identifier, and if the DOCTYPE is correctly placed as a document preamble, sets the Document to quirks mode.
error.missing-quote-before-doctype-system-iden: This error occurs if the parser encounters the DOCTYPE system identifier that is not preceded by a quote (e.g., <!DOCTYPE html SYSTEM http://www.w3.org/TR/xhtml1/DTD/xhtml1-transitional.dtd">). In such a case, the parser ignores the system identifier, and if the DOCTYPE is correctly placed as a document preamble, sets the Document to quirks mode.
error.missing-semicolon-after-character-refere: This error occurs if the parser encounters a character reference that is not terminated by a U+003B (;) code point. The parser behaves the same as if the character reference is terminated by the U+003B (;) code point. Most named character references require a terminating U+003B (;) code point. Those that don't might get resolved as a longer named character reference in certain ambiguous scenarios.
error.missing-whitespace-after-doctype-public-: This error occurs if the parser encounters a DOCTYPE whose "PUBLIC" keyword and public identifier are not separated by ASCII whitespace. In this case the parser behaves as if ASCII whitespace is present.
error.missing-whitespace-after-doctype-system-: This error occurs if the parser encounters a DOCTYPE whose "SYSTEM" keyword and system identifier are not separated by ASCII whitespace. In this case the parser behaves as if ASCII whitespace is present.
error.missing-whitespace-before-doctype-name: This error occurs if the parser encounters a DOCTYPE whose "DOCTYPE" keyword and name are not separated by ASCII whitespace. In this case the parser behaves as if ASCII whitespace is present.
error.missing-whitespace-between-attributes: This error occurs if the parser encounters attributes that are not separated by ASCII whitespace (e.g., '<div id="foo"class="bar">'). In this case the parser behaves as if ASCII whitespace is present.
error.missing-whitespace-between-doctype-publi: This error occurs if the parser encounters a DOCTYPE whose public and system identifiers are not separated by ASCII whitespace. In this case the parser behaves as if ASCII whitespace is present.
error.nested-comment: This error occurs if the parser encounters a nested comment (e.g., <!-- <!-- nested --> -->). Such a comment will be closed by the first occurring "-->" code point sequence and everything that follows will be treated as markup.
error.noncharacter-character-reference: This error occurs if the parser encounters a numeric character reference that references a noncharacter. The parser resolves such character references as-is.
error.noncharacter-in-input-stream: This error occurs if the input stream contains a noncharacter. Such code points are parsed as-is and usually, where parsing rules don't apply any additional restrictions, make their way into the DOM.
error.non-void-html-element-start-tag-with-tra: This error occurs if the parser encounters a start tag for an element that is not in the list of void elements or is not a part of foreign content (i.e., not an SVG or MathML element) that has a U+002F (/) code point right before the closing U+003E (>) code point. The parser behaves as if the U+002F (/) is not present.
error.null-character-reference: This error occurs if the parser encounters a numeric character reference that references a U+0000 NULL code point. The parser resolves such character references to a U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER.
error.surrogate-character-reference: This error occurs if the parser encounters a numeric character reference that references a surrogate. The parser resolves such character references to a U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER.
error.surrogate-in-input-stream: This error occurs if the input stream contains a surrogate. Such code points are parsed as-is and usually, where parsing rules don't apply any additional restrictions, make their way into the DOM. Surrogates can only find their way into the input stream via script APIs such as document.write().
error.unexpected-character-after-doctype-syste: This error occurs if the parser encounters any code points other than ASCII whitespace or closing U+003E (>) after the DOCTYPE system identifier. The parser ignores these code points.
error.unexpected-character-in-attribute-name: This error occurs if the parser encounters a U+0022 ("), U+0027 ('), or U+003C ('<') code point in an attribute name. The parser includes such code points in the attribute name. Code points that trigger this error are usually a part of another syntactic construct and can be a sign of a typo around the attribute name.
error.unexpected-character-in-unquoted-attribu: This error occurs if the parser encounters a U+0022 ("), U+0027 ('), U+003C ('<'), U+003D (=), or U+0060 (`) code point in an unquoted attribute value. The parser includes such code points in the attribute value. Code points that trigger this error are usually a part of another syntactic construct and can be a sign of a typo around the attribute value. U+0060 (`) is in the list of code points that trigger this error because certain legacy user agents treat it as a quote.
error.unexpected-equals-sign-before-attribute-: This error occurs if the parser encounters a U+003D (=) code point before an attribute name. In this case the parser treats U+003D (=) as the first code point of the attribute name. The common reason for this error is a forgotten attribute name.
error.unexpected-null-character: This error occurs if the parser encounters a U+0000 NULL code point in the input stream in certain positions. In general, such code points are either ignored or, for security reasons, replaced with a U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER.
error.unexpected-solidus-in-tag: This error occurs if the parser encounters a U+002F (/) code point that is not a part of a quoted attribute value and not immediately followed by a U+003E (>) code point in a tag (e.g., '<div / id="foo">'). In this case the parser behaves as if it encountered ASCII whitespace.
error.unknown-named-character-reference: This error occurs if the parser encounters an ambiguous ampersand. In this case the parser doesn't resolve the character reference.
error.missing-doctype: The document has no DOCTYPE. The standard calls a DOCTYPE a required preamble; without one the parser sets the document to quirks mode.
error.misplaced-doctype: A DOCTYPE appeared after the document had started. It is ignored; only a DOCTYPE at the very start sets the mode.
error.non-conforming-doctype: The DOCTYPE is not <!DOCTYPE html> (or one of the legacy strings the standard still permits). Depending on its public and system identifiers the document ends in quirks or limited-quirks mode.
error.end-tag-without-matching-open-element: An end tag closed an element that was not open. The parser ignores the tag.
error.closing-of-element-with-open-child-eleme: An end tag closed an element while child elements inside it were still open. The parser closes the children first (their end tags were missing or misnested).
error.disallowed-content-in-noscript-in-head: Content that is not allowed inside noscript in head (an element other than the metadata elements, or text) was found there. The parser closes the noscript and the head and moves on to the body.
error.open-elements-left-after-eof: The input ended while elements were still open. The parser closes them all; the missing end tags are supplied by the parser.
error.abandoned-head-element-child: A head-only element (base, link, meta, title, style, script, template or noscript) appeared after the head was closed and before the body started; the parser puts it back into the head.
error.misplaced-start-tag-for-head-element: A start tag for head itself appeared where it is not allowed (a second head, or one after the body). The parser ignores it.
error.nested-noscript-in-head: A noscript start tag appeared inside a noscript in head. The parser ignores it.
error.eof-in-element-that-can-contain-only-tex: The input ended inside an element whose content is text only (script, style, textarea, title). The parser closes the element at the end of the input.
error.unexpected-question-mark-instead-of-tag-: A question mark followed the less-than sign (<?...), the shape of an XML processing instruction, which HTML does not have. This parser treats it as a bogus comment up to the next greater-than sign; the current standard tokenizes processing instructions and names four errors for them, the first being disallowed-processing-instruction-target for an xml target, with the same comment as the outcome.

html-structure-explainer.errorsNote: The codes marked standard are the HTML Standard's own (13.2.2 Parse errors, where the descriptions are non-normative); the standard leaves the tree-construction errors unnamed and parse5, the parser used here, names those itself. Parse errors are syntax only: "Parse errors are only errors with the syntax of HTML." The error handling is defined, so a document with errors still has one exact tree, the one shown above.
html-structure-explainer.noFindings: Nothing to report: the document declares its type, language, title and encoding, its images have alternative text, its headings run in order, its ids are unique and its controls have labels.

ruleName.D2: A DOCTYPE that leaves quirks on
ruleName.D8: A link or button with no name
ruleName.D14: A formatting element split by the parser
ruleName.D15: Content moved out of a table
ruleName.D16: Void elements written with a trailing slash

finding.D1: There is no DOCTYPE, so the parser set the document to {mode} mode. The HTML Standard: "A DOCTYPE is a required preamble. DOCTYPEs are required for legacy reasons. When omitted, browsers tend to use a different rendering mode that is incompatible with some specifications." Write <!DOCTYPE html> as the first line.
finding.D2: The DOCTYPE is a legacy one and the document is in {mode} mode. The standard's parser puts a document in quirks or limited-quirks mode according to the DOCTYPE's public and system identifiers; <!DOCTYPE html> is the one that always yields no-quirks mode.

D3.missing: The root html element has no lang attribute. WCAG 2.2 SC 3.1.1 Language of Page (Level A): "The default human language of each web page can be programmatically determined." The HTML Standard: "Authors are encouraged to specify a lang attribute on the root html element, giving the document's language. This aids speech synthesis tools to determine what pronunciations to use, translation tools to determine what rules to use, and so forth."
D3.empty: The root html element has an empty lang attribute, which declares the language as unknown. WCAG 2.2 SC 3.1.1 Language of Page (Level A) asks that the default language be programmatically determinable; give lang a BCP 47 tag such as en or pt-BR.

D4.missing: There is no title element. The HTML Standard's content model for head, when no higher-level protocol supplies a title: "One or more elements of metadata content, of which exactly one is a title element". WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.2 Page Titled (Level A): "Web pages have titles that describe topic or purpose."
D4.several: There are {n} title elements. The HTML Standard: "There must be no more than one title element per document."
D4.empty: The title element is empty. WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.2 Page Titled (Level A): "Web pages have titles that describe topic or purpose."

D5.missing: No character encoding is declared in the document (no meta charset and no Content-Type meta). If the HTTP response does not declare one either, the browser sniffs the encoding. The HTML Standard requires documents to be UTF-8; '<meta charset="utf-8">' in the head says so in the file itself.
D5.late: The character encoding declaration ends {bytes} bytes into the document. The HTML Standard: "The element containing the character encoding declaration must be serialized completely within the first 1024 bytes of the document." Move it to the top of the head.
D5.not-utf8: The declared encoding is not UTF-8. The HTML Standard requires the document's encoding to be UTF-8 (the charset declaration is read, and legacy encodings still work, but new documents must be UTF-8).

finding.D6: {n, plural, one {One img element has} other {# img elements have}} no alt attribute (line {lines}). WCAG 2.2 SC 1.1.1 Non-text Content (Level A): "All non-text content that is presented to the user has a text alternative that serves the equivalent purpose". The HTML Standard: "Except where otherwise specified, the alt attribute must be specified and its value must not be empty", and for purely decorative images "the alt attribute must be present but must be empty". Note that an absent alt and an empty alt mean different things.
finding.D7: {n, plural, one {One img element carries} other {# img elements carry}} an empty alt, which marks the image as decorative or redundant beside its text. The HTML Standard: "In those cases, the alt attribute must be present but must be empty." Check that each of these images really conveys nothing the text does not.
finding.D8: This {element} element has no text and contains {images, plural, one {one image} other {# images}} without alternative text, so nothing names it. The HTML Standard: "When an a element that creates a hyperlink, or a button element, has no textual content but contains one or more images, the alt attributes must contain text that together convey the purpose of the link or button."

D9.jump: {n, plural, one {One heading jumps} other {# headings jump}} more than one level: an h{level} follows an h{prev}. The HTML Standard (4.3.11 Headings and outlines): "Each heading following another heading lead in the outline must have a heading level that is less than, equal to, or 1 greater than lead's heading level." WCAG 2.2 SC 1.3.1 Info and Relationships (Level A) asks that structure be programmatically determinable; a skipped level misstates the structure.
D9.no-h1: The document has {n, plural, one {one heading} other {# headings}} and none is an h1 (the first is an h{level}). The HTML Standard: "If a document has one or more headings, at least a single heading within the outline should have a heading level of 1."

finding.D10: The id "{id}" is used {n} times (lines {lines}). The HTML Standard: "When specified on HTML elements, the id attribute value must be unique amongst all the IDs in the element's tree". Labels, anchors, aria-labelledby and getElementById all resolve to the first one only.
finding.D11: The {element} element is obsolete. The HTML Standard (16.2 Non-conforming features): "Elements in the following list are entirely obsolete, and must not be used by authors". Browsers still render it for compatibility.
finding.D12: The {attr} attribute on {element} is obsolete. The HTML Standard (16.2): "The following attributes are obsolete (though the elements are still part of the language), and must not be used by authors".
finding.D13: {n, plural, one {One {element} element was} other {# {element} elements were}} closed by the parser, not by an end tag in the source, and {element} is not among the elements whose end tag the standard allows authors to omit (html, head, body, li, dt, dd, p, rt, rp, optgroup, option, colgroup, caption, thead, tbody, tfoot, tr, td, th). Either the end tag is missing or a later end tag closed this element first (misnesting). The tree shows where the parser ended it.
finding.D14: The {element} element starting at this position was split into {n} elements. When an end tag closes a formatting element (a, b, i, em, strong, font, small, s, u, code, nobr, big, tt, strike) that is not the innermost open element, the standard's adoption agency algorithm closes it and reopens a copy around the content that followed. Fix the nesting so each end tag closes the most recently opened element.
finding.D15: {n, plural, one {One node was} other {# nodes were}} moved before the table: text or elements written inside a table where only table parts (caption, colgroup, thead, tbody, tfoot, tr, td, th) may appear are inserted before the table by the standard's foster parenting rule. In the tree they appear ahead of the table they were written in.
finding.D16:
{n, plural, one {One void element is} other {# void elements are}} written with a trailing slash ('
'). The HTML Standard: "On void elements, it does not mark the start tag as self-closing but instead is unnecessary and has no effect of any kind. For such void elements, it should be used only with caution", because "if directly preceded by an unquoted attribute value, it becomes part of the attribute value". Harmless as written here.
finding.D17: This {element} control has no label: no label element wraps it or points at it with for, and no aria-label, aria-labelledby or title names it. The HTML Standard: "The caption can be associated with a specific form control, known as the label element's labeled control, either using the for attribute, or by putting the form control inside the label element itself." WCAG 2.2 SC 1.3.1 Info and Relationships (Level A) asks that the relationship be programmatically determinable.
finding.D18: Nothing ran: {scripts, plural, =0 {no script element} one {one script element} other {# script elements}}, {handlers, plural, =0 {no inline event handler} one {one inline event handler attribute} other {# inline event handler attributes}} and {urls, plural, =0 {no javascript: URL} one {one javascript: URL} other {# javascript: URLs}} were read as text and attributes only. This page parses; it never executes, fetches or renders.
finding.D19: {n, plural, one {One heading is} other {# headings are}} empty. WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.6 Headings and Labels (Level AA): "Headings and labels describe topic or purpose." An empty heading announces a section with no name.
finding.D20: The parser created {n, plural, one {one element} other {# elements}} that {n, plural, one {has} other {have}} no tag in the source: {names}. The HTML Standard: "Omitting an element's start tag in the situations described below does not mean the element is not present; it is implied, but it is still there." html, head, body and tbody are the usual ones.

obsoleteElement.applet: The standard says: use embed or object instead.
obsoleteElement.acronym: The standard says: use abbr instead.
obsoleteElement.bgsound: The standard says: use audio instead.
obsoleteElement.dir: The standard says: use ul instead.
obsoleteElement.frames: The standard says: either use iframe and CSS instead, or use server-side includes to generate complete pages with the various invariant parts merged in.
obsoleteElement.isindex: The standard says: use an explicit form and text control combination instead.
obsoleteElement.keygen: The standard says: for enterprise device management use cases, use native on-device management capabilities; for certificate enrolment use cases, use the Web Cryptography API to generate a keypair for the certificate.
obsoleteElement.listing: The standard says: use pre and code instead.
obsoleteElement.menuitem: The standard says: to implement a custom context menu, use script to handle the contextmenu event.
obsoleteElement.nextid: The standard says: use GUIDs instead.
obsoleteElement.noembed: The standard says: use object instead of embed when fallback is necessary.
obsoleteElement.param: The standard says: use the data attribute of the object element to set the URL of the external resource.
obsoleteElement.plaintext: The standard says: use the "text/plain" MIME type instead.
obsoleteElement.ruby: The standard says: providing the ruby base directly inside the ruby element or using nested ruby elements is sufficient.
obsoleteElement.strike: The standard says: use del instead if the element is marking an edit, otherwise use s instead.
obsoleteElement.xmp: The standard says: use pre and code instead, and escape "'<'" and "&" characters as "<" and "&".
obsoleteElement.presentational: The standard says: use appropriate elements or CSS instead. Where the tt element would have been used for marking up keyboard input, consider the kbd element; for variables, consider the var element; for computer code, consider the code element; and for computer output, consider the samp element. Similarly, if the big element is being used to denote a heading, consider using the h1 element; if it is being used for marking up important passages, consider the strong element; and if it is being used for highlighting text for reference purposes, consider the mark element.

obsoleteAttribute.charset-link: The standard says: use an HTTP Content-Type header on the linked resource instead.
obsoleteAttribute.charset-script: The standard says: omit the attribute. Both documents and scripts are required to use UTF-8, so it is redundant to specify it on the script element since it inherits from the document.
obsoleteAttribute.image-map-a: The standard says: use area instead of a for image maps.
obsoleteAttribute.methods: The standard says: use the HTTP OPTIONS feature instead.
obsoleteAttribute.name-id: The standard says: use the id attribute instead.
obsoleteAttribute.rev: The standard says: use the rel attribute instead, with an opposite term (for example, instead of rev="made", use rel="author").
obsoleteAttribute.urn: The standard says: specify the preferred persistent identifier using the href attribute instead.
obsoleteAttribute.form-accept: The standard says: use the accept attribute directly on the input elements instead.
obsoleteAttribute.area-useless: The standard says: these attributes do not do anything useful, and for historical reasons there are no corresponding IDL attributes on area elements. Omit them altogether.
obsoleteAttribute.nohref: The standard says: omitting the href attribute is sufficient; the nohref attribute is unnecessary. Omit it altogether.
obsoleteAttribute.profile: The standard says: unnecessary. Omit it altogether.
obsoleteAttribute.manifest: The standard says: use service workers instead.
obsoleteAttribute.version: The standard says: unnecessary. Omit it altogether.
obsoleteAttribute.ismap: The standard says: unnecessary. Omit it altogether. All input elements with a type attribute in the Image Button state are processed as server-side image maps.
obsoleteAttribute.usemap: The standard says: use the img element for image maps.
obsoleteAttribute.longdesc: The standard says: use a regular a element to link to the description, or (in the case of images) use an image map to provide a link from the image to the image's description.
obsoleteAttribute.lowsrc: The standard says: use a progressive JPEG image (given in the src attribute), instead of using two separate images.
obsoleteAttribute.link-target: The standard says: unnecessary. Omit it altogether.
obsoleteAttribute.menu-type: The standard says: to implement a custom context menu, use script to handle the contextmenu event. For toolbar menus, omit the attribute.
obsoleteAttribute.contextmenu: The standard says: to implement a custom context menu, use script to handle the contextmenu event.
obsoleteAttribute.scheme: The standard says: use only one scheme per field, or make the scheme declaration part of the value.
obsoleteAttribute.object-plugin: The standard says: use the data and type attributes to invoke plugins.
obsoleteAttribute.declare: The standard says: repeat the object element completely each time the resource is to be reused.
obsoleteAttribute.standby: The standard says: optimize the linked resource so that it loads quickly or, at least, incrementally.
obsoleteAttribute.typemustmatch: The standard says: avoid using object elements with untrusted resources.
obsoleteAttribute.language: The standard says: omit the attribute for JavaScript; for data blocks, use the type attribute instead.
obsoleteAttribute.script-event: The standard says: use DOM events mechanisms to register event listeners.
obsoleteAttribute.style-type: The standard says: omit the attribute for CSS; for data blocks, use script as the container instead of style.
obsoleteAttribute.datapagesize: The standard says: unnecessary. Omit it altogether.
obsoleteAttribute.summary: The standard says: use one of the techniques for describing tables given in the table section instead.
obsoleteAttribute.abbr: The standard says: use text that begins in an unambiguous and terse manner, and include any more elaborate text after that.
obsoleteAttribute.dropzone: The standard says: use script to handle the dragenter and dragover events instead.
obsoleteAttribute.css: The standard says: use CSS instead.

inert.scriptsValue: {n} ({external, plural, =0 {none external} one {one external} other {# external}})

html-structure-explainer.inertNote: This page builds the tree and reads it. Scripts are kept as text, event handler attributes as attributes, URLs as strings; no style is applied, no image, frame or script is fetched. The same parser runs in the hosted API with the same result.
html-structure-explainer.limits: The parser is parse5 8.0.1, which implements the HTML Standard's tokenizer and tree construction as of its release, with the scripting flag off (as DOMParser parses), so noscript content is read as elements. The standard's 2026 processing-instruction tokenization is not in it: <?…> is reported under the earlier name unexpected-question-mark-instead-of-tag-name and becomes a comment, which is also what the current standard does for an xml target. The findings read structure, not meaning: they cannot tell whether an alt text is a good one, whether a heading describes its section, or whether a lang tag is right; headingoffset and headingreset are not applied to the outline. Inputs over {max, number} characters are refused.

share.carries: The link carries the HTML as pasted; a page holding a key, token or password gets none.
share.caution: Pasted HTML can name internal hosts and paths: read it before you send the link.
share.maybeSecret: {more, plural, =0 {Line {line} may hold a secret ({label}): check it, and the rest of the page, before you send the link.} one {Line {line} ({label}) and one more line may hold secrets: check them, and the rest of the page, before you send the link.} other {Line {line} ({label}) and # more lines may hold secrets: check them, and the rest of the page, before you send the link.}}
share.blockedSecret: {more, plural, =0 {No link: line {line} holds a key, token or password ({label}). Replace it with a placeholder, then share again.} one {No link: line {line} ({label}) and one more line hold keys, tokens or passwords. Replace them with placeholders, then share again.} other {No link: line {line} ({label}) and # more lines hold keys, tokens or passwords. Replace them with placeholders, then share again.}}

err.tooLong: The HTML is {length, number} characters; the ceiling is {max, number}.

csp-evaluator.name: CSP evaluator
csp-evaluator.blurb: Paste a Content-Security-Policy, as a header value, a whole header line, a Report-Only header, a meta element or several at once, and read it the way CSP Level 3 reads it: each directive named and explained, each source expression classified by the grammar (keyword, nonce, hash, scheme, host and its wildcards), the effective source list per destination through the fallback chain, and a graded list of findings, each quoting the specification: 'unsafe-inline' and 'unsafe-eval', wildcard, data: and http: sources, missing object-src, base-uri and frame-ancestors, short nonces, 'strict-dynamic' without a nonce, keywords without quotes, missing semicolons, duplicate, unknown and obsolete directives, directives ignored in meta or in Report-Only, and whether the policy meets the specification's own Strict CSP. Decode and grade only, offline: nothing is fetched.
csp-evaluator.policyLabel: Policy (a header value, header lines, or a meta element)
csp-evaluator.noPolicy: No policy was found in the text: paste the header value, a Content-Security-Policy header line, or a meta element.

gradeText.strict: The policy meets the specification's Strict CSP (8.5): script by nonce or hash with 'strict-dynamic', no eval, base-uri pinned, the plugin sink closed.
gradeText.good: No high or medium finding: script is restricted without the known weak spots.
gradeText.fair: No high finding, but medium ones remain; see the list.
gradeText.weak: At least one high finding: the policy can be bypassed or does not do what it says.
gradeText.none: Nothing in the policy restricts script; against XSS it does nothing yet.

delivery.header: Read from a Content-Security-Policy header line.
delivery.report-only: Read from a Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only header line: monitored, not enforced.
delivery.meta: Read from a meta element: frame-ancestors, report-uri and sandbox do not apply there.

scriptInline.allowed: Inline script is allowed ('unsafe-inline' is not overridden).
scriptInline.nonce-hash: Inline script runs only with a matching nonce or hash.
scriptInline.unrestricted: Inline script is unrestricted (no script list at all).

csp-evaluator.scriptEval: {eval, select, yes {eval() is allowed} other {eval() is blocked}}; {wasm, select, yes {WebAssembly compilation is allowed} other {WebAssembly compilation is blocked}}.
csp-evaluator.scriptStrictDynamic: 'strict-dynamic' is on: hosts, schemes, 'self' and 'unsafe-inline' are ignored for script.
csp-evaluator.scriptNoncesHashes: {nonces, plural, =0 {No nonce} one {One nonce} other {# nonces}}, {hashes, plural, =0 {no hash} one {one hash} other {# hashes}} for script.
csp-evaluator.countsLine: Findings: {high, plural, =0 {no high} one {one high} other {# high}}, {medium, plural, =0 {no medium} one {one medium} other {# medium}}, {low, plural, =0 {no low} one {one low} other {# low}}, {info, plural, =0 {no notes} one {one note} other {# notes}}, {good, plural, =0 {nothing marked good} one {one thing done right} other {# things done right}}.

directive.child-src: Governs the creation of child navigables (frames) and worker contexts; frame-src and worker-src fall back to it (6.1.1).
directive.connect-src: Restricts the URLs script interfaces may connect to: fetch(), XMLHttpRequest, EventSource, sendBeacon, a ping, and WebSocket connections (6.1.2).
directive.default-src: The fallback for every fetch directive that is not set: "when default-src is set, every fetch directive that isn't explicitly set will fall back to the value default-src specifies." There is no inheritance: a directive that is set replaces it entirely (6.1.3).
directive.font-src: Restricts the URLs from which fonts may be loaded (6.1.4).
directive.frame-src: Restricts the URLs which may be loaded into child navigables (frames); falls back to child-src, then default-src (6.1.5).
directive.img-src: Restricts the URLs from which images may be loaded (6.1.6).
directive.manifest-src: Restricts the URLs from which application manifests may be loaded (6.1.7).
directive.media-src: Restricts the URLs from which video, audio and text tracks may be loaded (6.1.8).
directive.object-src: Restricts the URLs from which plugin content (object, embed) may be loaded; 'none' closes the sink entirely (6.1.9).
directive.script-src: Restricts the locations from which scripts may be executed: script requests, inline script blocks, inline event handlers (through script-src-attr's fallback), eval() and its kin (gated on 'unsafe-eval'), WebAssembly compilation (gated on 'wasm-unsafe-eval'), and worker scripts through worker-src's fallback (6.1.10).
directive.script-src-elem: Applies to script requests and script blocks only; inline event handlers are controlled by script-src-attr. Not used for the 'unsafe-eval' check and not a fallback for worker-src (6.1.11).
directive.script-src-attr: Applies to inline event handlers only (6.1.12).
directive.style-src: Restricts the locations from which style may be applied: stylesheet requests (link, @import, the Link header), inline style blocks and style attributes (6.1.13).
directive.style-src-elem: Applies to stylesheet requests and style elements only (6.1.14).
directive.webrtc: Restricts whether connections may be established via WebRTC: 'allow' or 'block' (6.2.1).
directive.worker-src: Restricts the URLs which may be loaded as a Worker, SharedWorker or ServiceWorker; falls back to child-src, then script-src, then default-src (6.2.2).
directive.base-uri: Restricts the URLs which can be used in a Document's base element. No fallback: without it, an injected base element can redirect every relative script URL (6.3.1).
directive.sandbox: Applies an HTML sandbox to the resource, as though it had been loaded in an iframe with a sandbox attribute; ignored in Report-Only and in meta (6.3.2).
directive.form-action: Restricts the URLs which can be used as the target of form submissions (6.4.1).
directive.frame-ancestors: Restricts the URLs which can embed the resource using frame, iframe, object or embed, against UI redressing; no fallback to default-src; ignored in meta (6.4.2).
directive.report-uri: Deprecated: the endpoints violation reports are sent to; ignored when report-to is present. The specification suggests specifying both for backwards compatibility (6.5.1).
directive.report-to: The Reporting API endpoint group violation reports are sent to (6.5.2).
directive.upgrade-insecure-requests: Instructs the user agent to upgrade insecure requests to HTTPS before fetching them (Upgrade Insecure Requests). Takes no value.
directive.require-trusted-types-for: Enforces Trusted Types at the DOM XSS injection sinks when its value is 'script' (Trusted Types 4.2.1).
directive.trusted-types: Controls which Trusted Type policies may be created: policy names, *, 'allow-duplicates', 'none' (Trusted Types 4.2.2).
directive.block-all-mixed-content: Obsolete. Mixed Content 6.1: "An earlier version of this specification defined the block-all-mixed-content CSP directive. It is now obsolete, because all mixed content is now blocked if it can't be autoupgraded."
directive.plugin-types: Not a directive of CSP Level 3 (Working Draft 16 September 2026); it appeared in earlier drafts and was removed. Browsers ignore directives they do not know.
directive.referrer: Not a directive of CSP Level 3; the Referrer-Policy header carries this now. Browsers ignore directives they do not know.
directive.reflected-xss: Not a directive of CSP Level 3; it appeared in earlier drafts and was removed. Browsers ignore directives they do not know.
directive.disown-opener: Not a directive of CSP Level 3; the Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy header carries this now. Browsers ignore directives they do not know.
directive.navigate-to: Not a directive of CSP Level 3; it appeared in earlier drafts and was removed. Browsers ignore directives they do not know.
directive.prefetch-src: Not a directive of CSP Level 3; it appeared in earlier drafts and was removed. Browsers ignore directives they do not know.
directive.require-sri-for: Not a directive of CSP Level 3; a separate draft once proposed it and it was never standardized. Browsers ignore directives they do not know.
directive.unknown: Not a directive of CSP Level 3 nor of a specification that extends it. Browsers ignore directives they do not know, so this one does nothing.

kind.nonce: a nonce-source: matches elements carrying this nonce
kind.hash: a hash-source: matches inline content with this digest
kind.scheme: a scheme-source: any URL of this scheme
kind.host: a host-source: a host, with optional scheme, port and path
kind.unquoted-keyword: a keyword written without quotes, read as a host
kind.directive-name: a directive name inside a value: a missing semicolon

keyword.self: the document's own origin, plus secure upgrades of it (https, wss on the default or matching port); blob: URLs never match it (6.7.2.8).
keyword.unsafe-inline: allows every inline script block, inline event handler, javascript: URL or inline style of the directive's type, unless a nonce or hash (or, for script, 'strict-dynamic') in the same list overrides it (6.7.3.2).
keyword.unsafe-eval: allows eval(), Function(), setTimeout and setInterval with a string, and WebAssembly compilation; a global page flag read from script-src or default-src (6.1.10).
keyword.strict-dynamic: host and scheme expressions, 'unsafe-inline' and 'self' are ignored for script; nonces and hashes are honoured; scripts loaded by trusted scripts (non-parser-inserted) are allowed (8.2).
keyword.unsafe-hashes: lets hash expressions match inline event handlers and javascript: URLs, not only script blocks (8.3).
keyword.report-sample: asks the user agent to include a sample of the violating inline content in violation reports.
keyword.unsafe-allow-redirects: allows redirects to be followed to destinations not otherwise in the list (a keyword the Working Draft still marks as an open issue).
keyword.wasm-unsafe-eval: allows WebAssembly compilation without allowing JavaScript eval() (6.1.10).
keyword.trusted-types-eval: allows the eval sinks when their argument is a TrustedScript (6.1.10).
keyword.report-sha256: asks for the SHA-256 of fetched scripts to be reported (4.1.4 Potentially report hash).
keyword.report-sha384: asks for the SHA-384 of fetched scripts to be reported (4.1.4).
keyword.report-sha512: asks for the SHA-512 of fetched scripts to be reported (4.1.4).
keyword.unsafe-webtransport-hashes: allows WebTransport connections with server certificate hashes.
keyword.block: WebRTC connections are blocked: no ICE candidates, no connectivity checks (6.2.1).
keyword.script: Trusted Types are required at the DOM XSS injection sinks (Trusted Types 4.2.1).
keyword.allow-duplicates: a Trusted Types policy name may be created more than once (Trusted Types 4.2.2).
keyword.none: no Trusted Types policy may be created (Trusted Types 4.2.2).

csp-evaluator.hostNote: a host-source: scheme {scheme}, host {host}{wildcard, select, yes { (a wildcard: it matches that host's subdomains, and their subdomains)} other {}}, port {port}, path {path}. A host without a scheme matches the page's scheme and its secure upgrade (6.7.2.8).
csp-evaluator.anyScheme: any (the page's own, or its secure upgrade)
csp-evaluator.schemeNote: a scheme-source: any URL whose scheme is {scheme}, on any host (6.7.2.8).
csp-evaluator.nonceNote: a nonce-source with {length, plural, one {{length} character} other {{length} characters}} of base64 value; it must change on every response and should encode at least 128 bits (7.1).
csp-evaluator.hashNote: a hash-source ({algorithm}): matches an inline block whose digest is this value; with 'unsafe-hashes', inline event handlers too.
csp-evaluator.effectiveIntro: What each destination is actually governed by, after the fallback list of 6.8.3 (script-src-elem falls back to script-src, then default-src; worker-src to child-src, script-src, default-src; frame-src to child-src, default-src; the others to default-src; base-uri, form-action and frame-ancestors never fall back).
csp-evaluator.effectiveNote: A directive that is set replaces the fallback entirely: "There is no inheritance" (6.1.3). An unrestricted row means no directive in the chain is present, so that destination may load from anywhere.

ruleName.C11: A value the directive does not take
ruleName.C17: A wildcard or bare scheme for script

finding.C1: A second {directive} directive appears later in the policy and the parser ignores it: "If policy's directive set contains a directive whose name is directive name, continue." Only the first one counts (2.2.1).
finding.C2: {directive} is not a directive of CSP Level 3 nor of any specification that extends it. Browsers ignore directives they do not know, so it adds nothing; check the spelling.

C3.block-all-mixed-content: block-all-mixed-content is obsolete: "all mixed content is now blocked if it can't be autoupgraded" (Mixed Content 6.1). It does nothing; upgrade-insecure-requests is the directive that still has an effect.
C3.plugin-types: plugin-types is not in CSP Level 3 (it was removed from the drafts). Use object-src 'none' to close the plugin sink.
C3.referrer: referrer is not in CSP Level 3. The Referrer-Policy response header carries this setting.
C3.reflected-xss: reflected-xss is not in CSP Level 3 (it was removed from the drafts). Browsers ignore it.
C3.disown-opener: disown-opener is not in CSP Level 3. The Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy response header carries this setting.
C3.navigate-to: navigate-to is not in CSP Level 3 (it was removed from the drafts). Browsers ignore it.
C3.prefetch-src: prefetch-src is not in CSP Level 3 (it was removed from the drafts). Browsers ignore it.
C3.require-sri-for: require-sri-for was proposed in a separate draft and never standardized. Browsers ignore it.

C4.yes: report-uri is deprecated and, since report-to is also present, it is ignored by browsers that support report-to: "If the latter directive is present, this directive will be ignored." Keeping both is what the specification suggests for older browsers (6.5.1).
C4.no: report-uri is deprecated: "Please use the report-to directive instead." The specification suggests specifying both for backwards compatibility (6.5.1).

C5.meta: {directive} is ignored when the policy is delivered in a meta element: "Neither are the report-uri, frame-ancestors, and sandbox directives" supported there (3.3). Deliver it in the Content-Security-Policy header.
C5.report-only: sandbox "will be ignored entirely when delivered in a Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only header" (6.3.2).

finding.C6: {value} is a directive name, but it sits inside the value of {directive}: a semicolon is missing before it. The parser reads it as a host-source (a server called "{value}") and the directive it was meant to start, with everything after it, never exists (2.2.1).
finding.C7: {value} is written without quotes, so the grammar reads it as a host named "{keyword}" rather than as the keyword, which must be written between single quotes: 'self', 'unsafe-inline', 'none' (2.3.1).
finding.C8: {value} matches none of the source-expression forms of 2.3.1 (keyword, nonce, hash, scheme, host). It cannot match any URL and is dead weight; check it for a typo.
finding.C9: 'none' is only meaningful alone: the grammar is "( source-expression *( required-ascii-whitespace source-expression ) ) / 'none'". Beside other expressions it matches nothing and changes nothing (2.3.1; 6.7.2.7).
finding.C10: {directive} has an empty value, which for a source-list directive means nothing matches, the same as 'none' ("The value MAY be empty", 2.3).

C11.webrtc: webrtc takes exactly one of 'allow' or 'block' (6.2.1); anything else is read as not 'allow', so connections are blocked.
C11.upgrade-insecure-requests: upgrade-insecure-requests takes no value (directive-value = ""); the tokens are ignored.
C11.require-trusted-types-for: require-trusted-types-for takes the keyword 'script' (Trusted Types 4.2.1); without it nothing is enforced.
C11.sandbox: {value} is not one of the iframe sandbox keywords the HTML Standard defines (allow-downloads, allow-forms, allow-modals, allow-orientation-lock, allow-pointer-lock, allow-popups, allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox, allow-presentation, allow-same-origin, allow-scripts, allow-top-navigation, allow-top-navigation-by-user-activation, allow-top-navigation-to-custom-protocols); each sandbox token "MUST be one of the keywords defined by HTML" (6.3.2).
C11.trusted-types-on: require-trusted-types-for 'script' is on: the DOM XSS injection sinks (innerHTML, eval, script src and the rest) accept only Trusted Types, which closes the DOM-based XSS class the rest of the policy cannot reach.

finding.C12: {value} is outside the frame-ancestors grammar: "ancestor-source = scheme-source / host-source / 'self'" (6.4.2). Nonces, hashes and the other keywords mean nothing here and are ignored.
finding.C13: No script-src, no script-src-elem and no default-src: nothing in this policy restricts where scripts come from or whether inline script runs. Against XSS the policy does nothing. Start from the specification's Strict CSP (8.5): script-src 'strict-dynamic' 'nonce-...'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'.

C14.no: 'unsafe-inline' in {directive} allows every inline script block, inline event handler and javascript: URL, which is what an XSS payload is. The specification's own reading: inline script is blocked "unless every policy allows inline script ... explicitly, by specifying 'unsafe-inline', a nonce-source or a hash-source" (6.1.10). Replace it with nonces or hashes; "nonces provide a substantial improvement over 'unsafe-inline'" (7.1).
C14.yes: 'unsafe-inline' in {directive} is overridden: a source list that contains a nonce, a hash or 'strict-dynamic' "Does Not Allow" all inline behaviour (6.7.3.2), so browsers that support CSP2 or later ignore the keyword. Kept this way it is a deliberate fallback for very old browsers, as 8.2 describes.
C14.hashes: 'unsafe-hashes' in {directive} lets hashes match inline event handlers and javascript: URLs. The specification: "hashes allow a particular script to execute, but do not ensure that it executes in the way a developer intends"; a handler like transferAllMyMoney() becomes injectable as a script block (8.3).
C14.style: 'unsafe-inline' in {directive} allows inline styles and style attributes. CSS injection is a lesser class than script injection, but it can exfiltrate data through selectors and background URLs; nonces or hashes work for style too.

C15.unsafe-eval: 'unsafe-eval' in {directive} allows eval(), Function(), and setTimeout or setInterval with a string: "The following JavaScript execution sinks are gated on the 'unsafe-eval' and 'trusted-types-eval' source expressions" (6.1.10). It is a global page flag, so an XSS that reaches any string sink becomes code.
C15.wasm-unsafe-eval: 'wasm-unsafe-eval' in {directive} allows WebAssembly compilation without allowing JavaScript eval() (6.1.10). Needed by WebAssembly applications; a much narrower grant than 'unsafe-eval'.
C15.trusted-types-eval: 'trusted-types-eval' in {directive} allows the eval sinks only for TrustedScript values (6.1.10): eval remains closed to plain strings.

finding.C16: 'strict-dynamic' is present in {directive} but no nonce and no hash is: with 'strict-dynamic', "host-source and scheme-source expressions, as well as the 'unsafe-inline' and 'self' keyword-sources will be ignored when loading script. hash-source and nonce-source expressions will be honored" (8.2). Nothing the parser inserts can run. Add the nonce or hash.

C17.scheme: {value} in {directive} allows script from any {scheme}: URL{sd, select, yes { (ignored here because 'strict-dynamic' is present, so this is the CSP2 fallback of 8.2)} other {}}. A bare scheme is an allowlist of the whole web, or, for data:, of whatever the attacker encodes inline; the specification's Strict CSP uses nonces or hashes instead and keeps https: only as a fallback behind 'strict-dynamic' (8.5).
C17.star: * in {directive} matches any HTTP(S) URL (6.7.2.8){sd, select, yes { (ignored here because 'strict-dynamic' is present)} other {}}: for script it is no restriction at all.

finding.C18: {directive} allows script by host ({value}{n, plural, =1 {} other { and more}}) without a nonce or hash. Host allowlists are the bypass class the specification itself describes: "Host- and path-based policies are tough to get right, especially on sprawling origins like CDNs" (8.2), and 8.5 recommends nonces or hashes with 'strict-dynamic' instead. Any JSONP endpoint, AngularJS copy or user-uploaded file on an allowed host executes.
finding.C19: 'self' for script allows everything served by the page's own origin. It is fine as long as that origin serves no JSONP endpoint, no AngularJS or similar framework the attacker can drive, and no user-uploaded content; otherwise it is the bypass 8.2 describes.

C20.missing: No object-src and no default-src: plugin content (object, embed) can be loaded from anywhere. Flash is gone, but the sink remains the way plugin-based XSS historically arrived; the specification notes that "developers can prevent the execution of arbitrary resources as plugin content by delivering the policy object-src 'none'" (6.1.9).
C20.open: {value} in {directive} leaves plugin content loadable from anywhere that matches. Close the sink: object-src 'none' (6.1.9).
C20.allowlist: Plugin content is allowed from {value} (through {directive}). Unless the page embeds plugins, object-src 'none' closes the sink entirely (6.1.9).
C20.none: object-src 'none': the plugin sink is closed, as the specification's Strict CSP examples do (8.5).

C21.missing: No base-uri. An injected '<base href>' rewrites every relative URL on the page, scripts included, and base-uri has no fallback to default-src. The specification's Strict CSP: "base-uri: Specify a value of either 'self' or 'none'" (8.5).
C21.open: base-uri {value} lets a base element point anywhere that matches, which lets an injected base element redirect relative script URLs. Use 'self' or 'none' (8.5).
C21.good: base-uri {value}: the base element is pinned, as Strict CSP asks (8.5).

C22.missing: No frame-ancestors: any site can embed this page in a frame, which is the clickjacking class frame-ancestors exists for (6.4.2). It does not fall back to default-src: "a policy that declares default-src 'none' will still allow the resource to be embedded by anyone." Add frame-ancestors 'none' or 'self' to the header (it is ignored in meta).

finding.C23: The nonce in {directive} has {length, plural, one {{length} character} other {{length} characters}} of base64 value, under the 22 that encode 128 bits: "The generated value SHOULD be at least 128 bits long (before encoding), and SHOULD be generated via a cryptographically secure random number generator" (7.1). A guessable or reused nonce defeats the whole list: "Nonces override the other restrictions present in the directive in which they're delivered."

C24.http: {value} in {directive} names an insecure scheme. The matching algorithm upgrades it ("script-src http: is treated as equivalent to script-src http: https:", 6.7.2.9), so https works, but the cleartext form is allowed too and can be tampered with in transit.
C24.ip: {value} in {directive} is an IP address. The host-part matching algorithm matches domains only: "If host is not a domain, return Does Not Match" (6.7.2.10); the specification notes that "only 127.0.0.1 will actually match a URL" (2.3.1). This expression never matches anything.
C24.localhost: {value} in {directive} allows the loopback address, the one IP address the matching algorithm accepts (2.3.1). Fine for development; remove it in production.

C25.none: No report-to and no report-uri: violations are blocked (or, in Report-Only, nothing happens) without anyone hearing of them. report-to names a Reporting API endpoint group (6.5.2); the specification suggests report-uri beside it for older browsers (6.5.1).
C25.report-to: report-to {value}: violation reports go to a Reporting API endpoint group (6.5.2).

finding.C26: This policy arrived in a Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only header: it is monitored, never enforced: "allows web developers to experiment with policies by monitoring (but not enforcing) their effects" (3.2). The findings describe what it would do if enforced; sandbox is ignored entirely in this mode (6.3.2).

csp-evaluator.handoff: The other security headers (HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, COOP and the rest) are read by the
csp-evaluator.limits: This page reads the policy's text against CSP Level 3 (W3C Working Draft, 16 September 2026) and grades it by the specification's own sentences; it does not fetch the page the policy protects, so it cannot know which inline scripts exist, whether a nonce really changes per response, or whether an allowed host serves JSONP. The host-allowlist findings are about the class, not a specific bypass. Several policies are evaluated one by one; when several are enforced, each must allow a load (8.1). Inputs over {max, number} characters are refused.

share.carries: The link carries the box as pasted; a box holding a credential or a cookie gets none.
share.caution: A policy can name internal hosts, and its nonces must never repeat: check it before you send the link.

Replace it with a placeholder, then share again.} one {No link: line {line} ({label}) and one more line hold credentials. Replace them with placeholders, then share again.} other {No link: line {line} ({label}) and # more lines hold credentials. Replace them with placeholders, then share again.}}

css-selector-tester.name: CSS selector tester
css-selector-tester.blurb: Paste HTML and one or more selectors (one per line) and see exactly which elements each selector matches: the elements highlighted in the parsed tree with their path and line, the count per selector, and its specificity counted per section 15 of Selectors Level 4. The HTML is parsed inertly with the same parser as the HTML structure explainer; the selectors are parsed and matched by Selectors Level 4's own rules (compound by compound, right to left), including :is(), :not(), :where(), :has(), :nth-child(An+B of S), attribute operators with the i and s flags, CSS escapes and the form-state pseudo-classes read from attributes. Invalid selectors are named with the position of the error; the pseudo-classes a static document cannot answer are marked. Checked against Chromium's querySelectorAll.

preset.static-document: What a static document cannot answer
preset.closed-at-the-end: Closed at the end of input

css-selector-tester.summary: {elements, plural, one {One element} other {# elements}}, {selectors, plural, =0 {no selectors} one {one selector} other {# selectors}}.
css-selector-tester.summaryMatches: {valid, plural, one {One valid} other {# valid}}, {invalid, plural, =0 {none invalid} one {one invalid} other {# invalid}}; {matched, plural, =0 {no element matched} one {one element matched} other {# elements matched}} by at least one selector.
css-selector-tester.quirksNote: The document is in {mode} mode (no DOCTYPE or a legacy one); matching is the same, the rendering would not be.
css-selector-tester.noSelectors: No selector yet: write one per line above.
css-selector-tester.focusTitle: Highlight only this selector's matches in the tree
css-selector-tester.matchCount: {n, plural, =0 {no match} one {one match} other {# matches}}
css-selector-tester.selectorsNote: A selector that names a pseudo-element (::before, ::first-line, …) selects a box, not an element; querySelectorAll returns nothing for it, and the count shown is of the elements that would originate the pseudo-element. The specificity is the triple of the most specific member of the list, counted per Selectors 4 section 15 from the parsed selector, so a member that a forgiving :is() or :where() dropped counts zero (16.1); the specificity calculator counts the text as written. Click a number to highlight one selector's matches in the tree.
css-selector-tester.moreMatches: and {n, plural, one {one more} other {# more}} (the tree marks them all)
css-selector-tester.treeIntroAll: Every element of the document the parser built, with the numbers of the selectors that match it. A dot in the gutter marks an element the parser created (html, head, body, tbody).
css-selector-tester.treeTruncated: The tree list stops at 2,000 elements; the counts cover the whole document.
css-selector-tester.handoff: The same tree, with the parser's repairs and errors, is in the
css-selector-tester.handoffSpecificity: and each selector's counting in the CSS specificity calculator
css-selector-tester.limits: The tester reads a static tree: no stylesheet is applied, no script runs, nothing is focused or hovered, nothing was visited, and :scope is the document root. :empty follows Chromium (Level 3) where Selectors Level 4 has moved on; the s flag and the quoted :lang() form follow Level 4 where Chromium has not (checked 2026-10-05). A selector left open at the end is closed there, as CSS Syntax does. Class and id match case-sensitively in every mode (the Quirks Mode Standard no longer defines a case quirk for them). Inputs over {max, number} characters of HTML are refused.

error.empty: Empty selector at position {at}: a selector list with an empty member is invalid (3.9), and matches nothing.
error.unexpected: Unexpected character at position {at}: not a token Selectors allows at this point, so the whole selector is invalid (3.9) and matches nothing.
error.bad-attr: The attribute selector at position {at} is malformed (a name, an operator and a value in quotes or as an identifier, optionally followed by i or s).
error.bad-nth: The argument at position {at} is not an An+B expression (13.3.1): even, odd, a number, or An+B such as 2n+1, -n+3, 10n-1.
error.bad-pseudo: The pseudo-class at position {at} lacks a valid argument.
error.pseudo-element-position: A pseudo-element must be the last part of a selector and there can be only one (3.6.1); position {at}.
error.pseudo-element-in-argument: A pseudo-element is not valid inside :is(), :where(), :not() or :has() (4.2 to 4.5): the argument at position {at} names one, so the selector is invalid.
error.dangling-combinator: A combinator with nothing after it at position {at}; the selector is invalid (3.9).
error.undeclared-namespace: The namespace prefix at position {at} is not declared, and a selector with an undeclared prefix is invalid (3.9); only *| and | are available here.
error.unknown-pseudo: A pseudo-class this tester does not know, at position {at}: a user agent "must treat as invalid any pseudo-classes ... for which they have no usable level of support" (3.9), so a browser that does not know it matches nothing either.

note.never: :{what} is valid but never matches here: "In non-interactive user agents, these pseudo-classes are valid, but never match any element" (section 9); :visited never matches by privacy; the resource, display and shadow-tree states have no meaning in a static tree.
note.static: :{what} depends on form state (constraint validation, placeholders, defaults) that this tester does not evaluate; a browser would. Treated as matching nothing.
note.approx: :{what} is read from attributes the way the HTML Standard defines it (checked, selected, disabled including a disabled fieldset's descendants outside its first legend, required, readonly, open, href on a or area, lang, dir, a hyphen in a custom element's name): a browser's answer can differ where scripts or user actions changed the state.
note.eof: The selector ends inside {what} without closing it. CSS Syntax closes a block, a function or a string at the end of input (sections 5.5.9, 5.5.10 and 4.3.5: "Discard a token from input. Return block"; for a string it is a parse error and the string is still returned), and Chromium (checked 2026-10-05) reads it that way; the selector is read as if closed.
note.level3: :empty follows the rule browsers apply (Selectors Level 3: any text of non-zero length makes an element non-empty). Selectors Level 4 (13.2) changes this so that whitespace-only text counts as empty; Chromium, checked 2026-10-05, does not yet.

share.carries: The link carries the HTML and the selectors as typed; a box holding a key, token or password gets none.
share.caution: Pasted HTML can name internal hosts and paths: read it before you send the link.
share.maybeSecret: {field, select, selectors {Line {line} of the selectors may hold a secret ({label}): check it before you send the link.} other {Line {line} of the HTML may hold a secret ({label}): check it, and the rest of the page, before you send the link.}}
share.blockedSecret: {field, select, selectors {No link: line {line} of the selectors holds a key, token or password ({label}). Replace it with a placeholder, then share again.} other {No link: line {line} of the HTML holds a key, token or password ({label}). Replace it with a placeholder, then share again.}}

err.htmlTooLong: The HTML is {length, number} characters; the ceiling is {max, number}.
err.selectorsTooLong: The selectors are {length, number} characters; the ceiling is {max, number}.

meta-og-jsonld-inspector.name: Meta, Open Graph & JSON-LD inspector
meta-og-jsonld-inspector.blurb: Paste a page, or just its head, and read everything it declares the way each standard reads it: the title and the character encoding by the HTML Standard, every meta element classified (the standard's own names, the WHATWG MetaExtensions registry, the pragma directives, the non-conforming ones), every link element with its rel tokens (canonical per RFC 6596, hreflang alternates, icons, manifest), the Open Graph object with its arrays and structured properties per ogp.me, the twitter:* card properties as registered, the robots and googlebot rules by Google's published list, the viewport, and every JSON-LD block parsed and outlined per JSON-LD 1.1. Forty-six findings, each quoting the sentence it rests on. Parsed inertly with parse5; nothing is fetched or executed.
meta-og-jsonld-inspector.inputLabel: HTML (a whole page, or just the head's contents)
meta-og-jsonld-inspector.placeholder:
'<'!DOCTYPE html>
'<html lang="en">'
'<head>'
'<meta charset="utf-8">'
'<title>'…'</title>'
'<meta name="description" content="…">'
'<link rel="canonical" href="https://…">'
'<meta property="og:title" content="…">'
'<script type="application/ld+json">''{…}''</script>'
'</head>'
meta-og-jsonld-inspector.summary: {metas, plural, =0 {No meta elements} one {One meta element} other {# meta elements}}, {links, plural, =0 {no link elements} one {one link element} other {# link elements}}, {og, plural, =0 {no Open Graph properties} one {one Open Graph property} other {# Open Graph properties}}, {twitter, plural, =0 {no twitter:* properties} one {one twitter:* property} other {# twitter:* properties}}, {jsonld, plural, =0 {no JSON-LD blocks} one {one JSON-LD block} other {# JSON-LD blocks}}.
meta-og-jsonld-inspector.summaryFindings: {errors, plural, =0 {No errors} one {One error} other {# errors}}, {warnings, plural, =0 {no warnings} one {one warning} other {# warnings}}, {infos, plural, =0 {no notes} one {one note} other {# notes}}, {goods, plural, =0 {nothing marked in order} one {one thing in order} other {# things in order}}.

ruleName.M20: Open Graph property outside ogp.me's list
ruleName.M23: twitter:card value outside the registry's four
ruleName.M24: twitter:* name not in the registry
ruleName.M25: JSON-LD block is not valid JSON
