bigip-scripted-monitor-explainer.name: BIG-IP Scripted monitor explainer
bigip-scripted-monitor-explainer.blurb: Paste the send and expect file a BIG-IP LTM Scripted monitor reads and see each line as the monitor reads it, with findings against every rule F5 states (LF line endings, exactly one space after the keyword, nothing after a closing quotation mark, a match only on a prefix of the reply, its escape sequences) and against what F5 leaves open. Add a server transcript in the RFCs' S: and C: notation and the check is simulated line by line: pass, fail at a line and why, or undetermined where F5's text does not say. Nothing connects anywhere.
bigip-scripted-monitor-explainer.scriptLabel: The script file (send and expect lines)
bigip-scripted-monitor-explainer.transcriptPlaceholder:
S: 220 mail.example.net ESMTP ready
C: HELO bigip1.example.net
S: 250 mail.example.net
C: QUIT
S: 221 mail.example.net closing
bigip-scripted-monitor-explainer.transcriptHelp: Write the session as the RFCs do: S: before each line the server sends, C: before each line the client sends. A reply is a run of S: lines; a C: line or a blank line ends it. Each S: line is read as ending in CR LF, as SMTP, POP3, IMAP and FTP require, and the blanks after S: and C: are notation, not data.
bigip-scripted-monitor-explainer.runsLocally: Runs in your browser. The script and the transcript never leave the page, and nothing connects to any server.
bigip-scripted-monitor-explainer.tooLongScript: The script is longer than {max, number} characters; a monitor script is a few lines.
bigip-scripted-monitor-explainer.tooLongTranscript: The transcript is longer than {max, number} characters.
bigip-scripted-monitor-explainer.statFindings: {error, plural, one {# error} other {# errors}}, {warning, plural, one {# warning} other {# warnings}}, {info, plural, one {# note} other {# notes}}
bigip-scripted-monitor-explainer.statNoLf: no LF at the end of the file
bigip-scripted-monitor-explainer.noTranscript: Paste a server transcript to simulate the check line by line.
bigip-scripted-monitor-explainer.verdictPass: Passes: every line ran and every expect matched the start of its reply.

reason.not-prefix: the text appears in the reply, but at character {at}, not at its start. F5: matching text can match the prefix of a response, but cannot match a substring that is not a prefix.
reason.mismatch: the reply does not start with the text, and does not contain it. F5 matches only a prefix of the response.
reason.reply-shorter: the reply ends before the text does, so the text cannot be its prefix; the monitor would wait for more until the Timeout runs out.
reason.after-quote: characters follow the closing quotation mark. F5: any characters that follow a closing quotation mark will break the match.
reason.crlf-after-quote: the line ends in CR LF, and the CR follows the closing quotation mark. F5: scripts must use LF line endings, and any characters after a closing quotation mark will break the match.
reason.no-reply: the transcript has no further reply, so the server sends nothing. F5: a target that does not respond within the Timeout is considered down.
reason.crlf: the line holds a CR. F5 says scripts must use LF line endings, not CR-LF, but not how such a line is then read.
reason.separator: the keyword is not followed by exactly one space, which F5 requires; what the monitor then reads is not documented.
reason.leading-space: white space comes before the keyword, which F5 does not describe.
reason.unknown-keyword: the line does not start with send or expect, the only keywords F5 documents.
reason.unknown-escape: the text holds an escape sequence that is not in F5's list.
reason.quote-form: the text uses a quotation form F5 does not describe.
reason.empty-text: the line has no text, and F5 does not say what an empty send or expect does.
reason.blank-line: a blank line comes between instructions, and F5 does not say how blank lines are read.
reason.send-after-quote: characters follow the send's closing quotation mark; F5 says they break a match, but not what a send line then sends.
reason.last-line-no-lf: this expect is on the last line, which has no LF; F5 does not say whether such a line is read.
reason.case-only: the reply starts with the same text in another case; F5 does not say whether the comparison is case-sensitive.
reason.spans-lines: the text matches only if the monitor has read past the end of the reply's first line, and F5 does not say how much of a reply it reads before comparing.
reason.no-expect: the script has no expect line, so nothing the server says is checked, and F5 does not say what decides the result.

bigip-scripted-monitor-explainer.clientDiffers: the transcript shows the client sending {client}

note.trailing-blank: The file ends with blank lines. They come after the last instruction, so they cannot change a match; F5 does not say how blank lines are read.
note.last-send-no-lf: The last line, a send, has no LF. It cannot change a match; F5 does not say whether such a line is read.
note.client-differs: At least one send differs from the client line the transcript shows, so the transcript may come from another client; the replies are compared as given.

bigip-scripted-monitor-explainer.noteUnread: {n, plural, one {# server reply was} other {# server replies were}} never read by an expect.
bigip-scripted-monitor-explainer.noteUnused: {n, plural, one {# client line in the transcript was} other {# client lines in the transcript were}} not matched with a send.
bigip-scripted-monitor-explainer.noteIgnored: Ignored transcript lines (they start with neither S: nor C:): {lines}.
bigip-scripted-monitor-explainer.assumption: The one assumption the simulator makes: each expect is compared with the next server reply of the transcript. F5 does not say what counts as a response when a reply has several lines; wherever that could change the verdict, the simulator says undetermined instead of guessing.
bigip-scripted-monitor-explainer.timing: The timing is the monitor's, not the script's: with F5's defaults a Scripted monitor checks every 10 seconds (Interval), and a target that does not respond within the Timeout of 31 seconds, three times the Interval plus one, is considered down.
bigip-scripted-monitor-explainer.linesTitle: Each line, as the monitor reads it
bigip-scripted-monitor-explainer.kindSend: Sends {length, plural, one {# character} other {# characters}}: {text}.
bigip-scripted-monitor-explainer.kindExpect: Checks that the reply starts with {length, plural, one {this character} other {these # characters}}: {text}.
bigip-scripted-monitor-explainer.kindOpen: A {keyword} line whose text F5's rules do not settle (see the findings).
bigip-scripted-monitor-explainer.lineBreaks: F5: the characters after the closing quotation mark break the match, so this expect cannot match.

ending.crlf: It ends with CR LF, the line ending SMTP, POP3, IMAP and FTP use.
ending.none: It ends with no line ending.

hint.reply-220: 220 is the greeting of SMTP (RFC 5321 4.3.2) and of FTP (RFC 959 5.4).
hint.reply-221: 221 is the reply to QUIT in SMTP (RFC 5321 4.1.1.10) and in FTP (RFC 959 4.2).
hint.reply-250: 250 is the SMTP success reply, for example to HELO or EHLO (RFC 5321 4.3.2).
hint.reply-554: 554 at connection time is an SMTP server refusing the session (RFC 5321 3.1).
hint.reply-421: 421 is service not available, closing the channel (RFC 5321 4.2.2, RFC 959 4.2).
hint.reply-120: 120 is the FTP reply for service ready in so many minutes, which can come before 220 (RFC 959 5.4).
hint.reply-230: 230 is the FTP reply for user logged in (RFC 959 4.2).
hint.reply-331: 331 is the FTP reply for user name okay, need password (RFC 959 4.2).
hint.reply-pop-ok: +OK is the POP3 positive status indicator, always sent in upper case (RFC 1939 section 3).
hint.reply-pop-err: -ERR is the POP3 negative status indicator (RFC 1939 section 3).
hint.reply-imap-ok: * OK is the IMAP untagged OK; as a greeting it says the connection is not yet authenticated (RFC 9051 7.1.1).
hint.reply-imap-preauth: * PREAUTH is the IMAP greeting of a pre-authenticated connection (RFC 9051 7.1.4).
hint.reply-imap-bye: * BYE is the IMAP BYE response: part of a logout, or a greeting that refuses the connection (RFC 9051 7.1.5).
hint.cmd-helo: HELO identifies the client to an SMTP server (RFC 5321 4.1.1.1).
hint.cmd-ehlo: EHLO identifies the client to an SMTP server and asks for its extensions; the reply is normally several lines (RFC 5321 4.1.1.1).
hint.cmd-quit: QUIT ends the session in SMTP (RFC 5321 4.1.1.10), POP3 (RFC 1939 section 4) and FTP (RFC 959).
hint.cmd-noop: NOOP only asks for a reply (RFC 5321 4.1.1.9, RFC 1939 section 5).
hint.cmd-user: USER names the user in POP3 (RFC 1939 section 7) and FTP (RFC 959).
hint.cmd-pass: PASS sends the password in POP3 (RFC 1939 section 7) and FTP (RFC 959).
hint.cmd-imap-logout: LOGOUT: the server sends an untagged BYE, then the tagged OK, then closes the connection (RFC 9051 6.1.3).
hint.cmd-imap-capability: CAPABILITY lists what the server supports, before the tagged OK (RFC 9051 6.1.1).
hint.cmd-imap-noop: NOOP only asks for a reply (RFC 9051 6.1.2).

bigip-scripted-monitor-explainer.picturesNote: In the As written column, a control character the file really holds (the CR of a CR-LF line ending, a tab) is shown as its Unicode picture, such as ␍ or ␉, while an escape typed as a backslash and a letter stays as typed. Elsewhere, text is shown with F5's escape sequences, and a backslash in the text as two backslashes.
bigip-scripted-monitor-explainer.clean: No findings: every rule F5 states is kept, and nothing F5 leaves open is used.

rule.S1: {what, select, crlf {This line ends in CR LF.} other {This line holds a CR character.}} F5: scripts must use hard-return line endings (LF), not soft-return line endings (CR-LF). Save the file with LF line endings.
rule.S2: {what, select, tab {A tab follows the keyword.} other {{count} spaces follow the keyword.}} F5: exactly one character space must separate send or expect from the text.
rule.S3: Characters follow the closing quotation mark: {after}. F5: any characters that follow a closing quotation mark will break the match. {kind, select, send {What a send line then sends is not documented.} other {This expect cannot match.}}
rule.S4: {keyword} is not a keyword F5 documents: a Scripted monitor file holds send and expect lines. {what, select, case {F5 writes the keywords in lower case.} comment {F5 describes no comment syntax.} tcl {This looks like an Expect (Tcl) script, which is a different language.} other {Remove the line or start it with send or expect.}}
rule.S5: {seq} is not one of the escape sequences F5 lists ({list}); what the monitor makes of it is not documented.
rule.S6: This send ends with no line ending. SMTP, POP3, IMAP and FTP end every command with CR LF (RFC 5321 2.3.8, RFC 1939 section 3, RFC 9051 2.2, RFC 959 section 4), so a server of those protocols waits for one; end the text with the escapes for CR and LF.
rule.S7: {what, select, lf {This send ends in LF alone} other {This send ends in CR alone}}, where SMTP, POP3, IMAP and FTP use CR LF; RFC 5321 2.3.8 says a conforming implementation must not recognize any other line terminator.
rule.S8: {text} is matched literally, as a prefix: a Scripted monitor has no wildcards and no regular expressions (F5: only the HTTP, HTTPS, HTTP/2, TCP and UDP monitors support regular expression matching).
rule.S9: {trailing, select, 1 {A blank line after the last instruction.} other {A blank line between instructions.}} F5 does not say how blank lines are read; leave them out.
rule.S10: White space before the keyword. F5 does not describe it; start the line with send or expect.
rule.S11: {what, select, single {Single quotation marks: F5 lists an escape for the single quotation mark but does not say whether single quotation marks enclose a text.} unterminated {An opening quotation mark with no closing one.} other {A quotation mark inside an unquoted text.}} F5 does not say how this is read.
rule.S12: This line has no text. F5 does not say what an empty send or expect does.
rule.S13: The last line has no LF. F5 requires LF line endings but does not say whether a last line without one is read; end the file with a line break.
rule.S14: No expect line: the script never checks anything the server says, and F5 does not say what decides the result of such a script.
rule.S15: This send carries a password ({text}). The file in /config/eav/ keeps it in clear text, and the tmsh reference lists no TLS option for this monitor type; RFC 9051 6.2.3 says LOGIN must not be used on unsecure networks. Where the protocol allows it, check the service without logging in, with QUIT or LOGOUT before authentication.
rule.S16: {code} followed by a space never starts a multi-line reply: every line but the last begins with the code and a hyphen (RFC 5321 4.2.1, RFC 959 4.2). If the reply can have several lines, expect the code alone.

bigip-scripted-monitor-explainer.limits: What this explainer cannot know: what a BIG-IP reads beyond F5's published rules, how your server really answers (the transcript is yours), and the monitor's timing. Test the monitor on the system itself, for example with tmsh run ltm monitor scripted my_monitor destination 192.0.2.10:25 and then show ltm monitor scripted my_monitor test-result, or with the Test tab in the Configuration utility.

share.carries: The link carries both boxes with every PASS and LOGIN password replaced by the bullets this page shows.
share.caution: Other credentials, such as an SMTP AUTH exchange, go as typed: check both boxes before you send the link.
share.blockedEscaped: No link: the password on line {line} is written with escape sequences, so it cannot be replaced safely.

expect-script-builder.name: Expect script builder
expect-script-builder.blurb: Choose ssh, telnet or another program, how to log in, a device profile (Cisco IOS XE, F5 BIG-IP tmsh, FortiOS, Extreme Switch Engine and Fabric Engine, or your own prompt) and the commands, and get a complete Expect script that logs in, deals with paging, runs them and logs out, changing nothing on the device unless you ask (on FortiOS it answers --More-- rather than change a global setting). No password is ever written into it, nothing secret reaches a log, ssh checks host keys with accept-new, and every script it writes passes the Expect script explainer with no error and no warning.

field.userOptional: User (if the program asks for one)
field.hostFromArgv: Take the host from the command line (expect script.exp HOST)
field.enableVar: Environment variable with the enable password
field.restorePaging: Put the paging setting back at the end

auth.ask: Password asked for when the script runs

authHelp.key: ssh runs with BatchMode=yes: it never asks for a password, so the key must work on its own (from ssh-agent, or a key without a passphrase).
authHelp.env: The script reads the password from the environment, checks that it is there, and removes it from the environment before starting ssh, telnet or the program.
authHelp.ask: The script asks for the password with echo off when it runs, the way expect(1) shows, so it needs a terminal.
authHelp.none: The program is already logged in or asks for nothing; the script waits for its prompt.

expect-script-builder.profileFacts: Prompts, paging and enable from {documented}, read on {readOn}.

enable.env: enable, password from an environment variable
enable.ask: enable, password asked for when the script runs

output.both: On the screen and in a log file

expect-script-builder.errorsTitle: The script cannot be written yet:

host.required: Give the host, or take it from the command line.
host.invalid: The host must be a host name or an address: letters, digits, dots, colons and hyphens, not starting with a hyphen.

port.not-for-transport: A port is set for ssh only; for telnet on another port, use Another program.
port.invalid: The port must be a number from 1 to 65535.

user.required: telnet answers the login question with a user name: give one.
user.invalid: The user name may hold letters, digits and . _ @ -, and may not start with a hyphen.

program.required: Give the program to start, with its arguments.
program.too-many: Up to {max} words on the program's command line.
program.invalid: The program's command line may hold letters, digits and . _ / : = @ , + % -, words separated by spaces, and may not start with a hyphen (nothing Tcl would substitute).

auth.not-for-transport: A key works with ssh only, and None with another program only.

keyFile.invalid: The key file must be a plain path (letters, digits, . _ / -, no spaces and no ~).

passwordVar.invalid: The variable name must start with a letter or an underscore and hold letters, digits and underscores.

genericPrompt.invalid: The prompt regexp must be one line of up to 200 characters.
genericPrompt.unbalanced: The prompt regexp's braces must balance, since it is written between braces.
genericPrompt.too-broad: That regexp matches anything at once and would never wait for the prompt (the explainer's rule E3).

genericPagingCommand.invalid: The paging command must be one line of up to 300 characters.

enable.not-for-profile: This profile has no enable step.
enable.no-password-prompt: The documents read for this profile do not print enable's password question, so the script cannot answer it: choose enable with no password asked.

enableVar.invalid: The variable name must start with a letter or an underscore and hold letters, digits and underscores.

paging.not-for-profile: That paging choice is not available for this profile (answering needs a more prompt the vendor documents).
paging.required: Give the command that turns paging off, or choose Nothing.

commands.control-character: Command {n} holds a control character (a tab, for example); commands must be plain text.

loginTimeout.invalid: The login timeout must be a whole number of seconds from 1 to {max}.

commandTimeout.invalid: The command timeout must be a whole number of seconds from 1 to {max}.

logFile.invalid: The log file must be a plain path (letters, digits, . _ / -, no spaces and no ~).

logout.invalid: The logout command must be one line of up to 64 characters.

expect-script-builder.scriptTitle: The script ({lines, plural, one {{lines} line} other {{lines} lines}})
expect-script-builder.verdict: The Expect script explainer reads it here: {error, plural, one {# error} other {# errors}}, {warning, plural, one {# warning} other {# warnings}}, {info, plural, one {# note} other {# notes}}.

note.paging-global: set output standard is a global configuration change: every administrator's CLI session sees it, not only this one. {restore, select, yes {The script puts it back at the end ({commands}).} other {The script leaves it changed; to put it back: {commands}.}} If the script stops early (status 3 or 4), the restore does not run. The default, Answer --More-- with Space, changes nothing.
note.paging-preference: tmsh keeps pager disabled as a cli preference of this user; the reference does not say how long it lasts or give a value to restore, so read list /cli preference first if it must be put back.
note.paging-unstated: The reference does not state how long terminal more disable lasts. {restore, select, yes {The script turns it back on at the end.} other {The script leaves it as it is.}}
note.telnet-clear: telnet carries the password as it is typed: RFC 854 defines no encryption. Prefer ssh, which ssh(1) describes as providing secure encrypted communications over an insecure network.
note.key-batchmode: With BatchMode=yes, ssh asks nothing: ssh_config(5) says it disables user interaction such as password prompts and host key confirmation, for scripts. A key whose passphrase must be typed cannot be used that way, so load it into ssh-agent first; a refused key ends the login with status 1.
note.ask-terminal: The password is asked for with echo off when the script runs, so run it at a terminal, not from cron.
note.env-run: Set {vars} in the environment of the shell that runs the script; the script checks it and removes it from the environment before starting the connection.
note.confirmation: "{command}" asks "{prompt}" (documented answer: {answer}). The script does not answer questions: it stops with status 3 when the command timeout passes. Answering on purpose belongs in a script you write yourself.
note.generic-prompt: Generic profile: the script waits for the prompt regexp you gave after login and after every command; check it against your device's prompt in every mode the commands reach.
note.log-file: The log file {file} is opened after the login, so the login and its password stay out of it; it holds whatever the device prints, configurations included, so keep it where only you can read it.
note.quiet: Nothing reaches the screen: the explainer notes log_user 0 left in place (E12), which is what a file-only script means.
note.more-answer: The script answers each --More-- with a Space, which the pager reads as one key: the explainer notes the send without a return (E5), which is right here.
note.enable-unprompted: On {platform}, enable can ask for a user name and a password depending on configuration, and the documents read do not print those questions; if it asks, the script stops with status 1.
note.argv-host: The host comes from the script's first argument and is checked before use: anything but a host name or an address stops the script with status 2, so it can never reach ssh as an option.
note.close-instead: No logout command: the script closes the connection and waits for the program to end.
note.paging-unchanged: Nothing on the device changes: the script answers each --More-- with a Space and keeps waiting. Turning paging off instead ({commands}) is a global configuration change that every administrator's session would see, so it is a choice you make explicitly.

expect-script-builder.pagingGlobalAnswer: The default answers --More-- and changes nothing on the device. Turning paging off is a global configuration change.
expect-script-builder.pagingGlobalOff: Turning paging off changes the device's global configuration for every administrator; the script puts it back at the end if you keep the restore.
expect-script-builder.runTerminal: Run it at a terminal: it asks for a password.

exit.login: the login failed (no prompt in time, the connection closed, or a password refused)
exit.input: missing or wrong input (an unset variable, a bad host argument, no password typed)
exit.command: a command did not finish (silence longer than the command timeout, a question nobody answered)
exit.closed: the session closed while a command or enable was running

section.header: What the script does, how to run it, where its secrets come from, and its exit statuses.
section.timeout: The timeout for each login step, set before the first expect so no expect runs on the default of 10 seconds.
section.target: The host (fixed, or from the command line and checked) and the user.
section.secret-env: The password from the environment: present and not empty, or the script stops; then removed from the environment so no program the script starts inherits it.
section.secret-ask: The password asked for with echo off, the expect(1) idiom, with its own two minutes to type it; echo comes back on in every case.
section.enable-env: The enable password from the environment, checked and removed the same way.
section.enable-ask: The enable password asked for with echo off.
section.quiet: log_user 0: the login stays off the screen, so nothing a device echoes there can be seen.
section.spawn: The connection: ssh with StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new (and BatchMode with a key), telnet, or the program.
section.login: One expect for the whole login: each question is answered once (a second one means it was refused), the prompt ends it, and timeout and eof stop the script with status 1.
section.enable: enable, its password question answered once, then the privileged prompt.
section.command-proc: run_command: send one line with a return, then wait for the prompt; each line of output restarts the timer (exp_continue), so the timeout counts silence.
section.command-timeout: The timeout for each command, at the top level, after the login.
section.paging: The profile's commands that turn paging off, each waited for like any command.
section.output: From here on the session goes to the screen, to the log file, or both; the file is opened only now.
section.commands: Your commands, each sent as typed (Tcl's special characters protected).
section.restore: The paging setting put back with the vendor's documented commands.
section.logout: The logout command and the end of the connection (or a close), then wait, so the process is reaped.

expect-script-builder.limits: The builder writes the script in your browser and never runs it. It does not answer questions a command asks, does not handle a prompt the profile's pattern misses (a banner or a command line that ends in > or #, for example), and writes comments and messages in English, like the commands themselves. Run the script against a lab device first.

share.carries: The link carries the form's choices and fields, never the script; a credential in a field stops it.
share.caution: The form names your host, user and commands: read them before you send the link.
share.maybeSecret: {field, select, commands {Line {line} of the commands} program {The program line} host {The host} user {The user} other {A field of the form}} may hold a secret ({label}){more, plural, =0 {} one {, and one more place may too} other {, and # more places may too}}: check before you send the link.
share.blockedSecret: No link: {field, select, commands {line {line} of the commands} program {the program line} host {the host} user {the user} other {a field of the form}} holds a credential ({label}){more, plural, =0 {} one {, and one more place does} other {, and # more places do}}. Replace it with a placeholder, then share again.

python-traceback-explainer.name: Python traceback explainer
python-traceback-explainer.blurb: Paste a CPython traceback: every frame, the markers, the exception against the built-in hierarchy, chains, exception groups and notes, where to look first, and a redacted copy to share.
python-traceback-explainer.inputPlaceholder: Paste a traceback, from "Traceback (most recent call last):" to the exception line
python-traceback-explainer.runsLocally: Read in your browser and never sent anywhere. A traceback can hold user names, host names and tokens, so this page never puts it in a link as pasted: Share results carries the redacted copy only.

errors.empty: The box is empty.
errors.too-long: The paste has {length, number} characters; the limit is {max, number}. Paste one traceback, not a whole log.
errors.too-many-lines: The paste has {lines, number} lines; the limit is {max, number}.
errors.line-too-long: Line {line, number} is longer than {max, number} characters.
errors.no-traceback: No CPython traceback was found: no "Traceback (most recent call last):" header, no exception group box, no SyntaxError location and no exception line.
errors.too-deep: The exception groups are nested deeper than {max, number} levels. CPython itself prints ten by default.

notes.bom-removed: A byte order mark at the start was removed.
notes.crlf: CR LF line breaks were read as LF.
notes.colour-removed: {n, plural, one {# colour code was} other {# colour codes were}} removed. From 3.13 CPython colours tracebacks on a terminal; PYTHON_COLORS=0 or NO_COLOR turns it off.
notes.nbsp: On {n, plural, one {# line} other {# lines}}, no-break spaces in the indentation were read as spaces (chat apps paste them).
notes.indented: The whole traceback was indented {n, number} spaces; the indentation was removed before reading.
notes.preamble: {n, plural, one {# line} other {# lines}} before the traceback {n, plural, one {was} other {were}} not read.
notes.thread: Line {line, number} says the exception was raised in a thread: threading.excepthook printed it, and the program may have carried on.
notes.unraisable: Line {line, number} says "Exception ignored": sys.unraisablehook printed an exception that could not propagate (in a destructor, for example), and the program carried on.
notes.another-traceback: Another traceback starts at line {line, number}; paste it on its own to read it.
notes.trailing: {n, plural, one {# line} other {# lines}} after the traceback {n, plural, one {was} other {were}} not read.
notes.incomplete: The traceback stops at line {line, number} without its exception line: the paste looks cut.
notes.extra-lines: {n, plural, one {One exception has} other {# exceptions have}} lines after the exception line (the first at line {line, number}). They are the rest of a message that has line breaks, or notes added with add_note(); the text alone cannot tell which.
notes.locals: Local variables were printed under {n, plural, one {# frame} other {# frames}} (unittest --locals or capture_locals), the first at line {line, number}. Their values can hold secrets.
notes.no-markers: The frames show source lines but no ^ or ~ markers. Either the release is older than 3.11, the interpreter ran with -X no_debug_ranges or PYTHONNODEBUGRANGES, or every expression covered its whole line.
notes.marker-mismatch: The markers under the frame at line {line, number} run past the end of its source line; the marked text may be off.
notes.group-count: The group at line {line, number} says it has {declared, number} sub-exceptions, but {shown, number} are shown.
notes.foreign-format: This looks like another tool's report (IPython or pytest), not CPython's own traceback. Only lines in CPython's format are read; run the code with python itself to get one.
notes.sensitive: The paste holds something that may be sensitive.
notes.secrets-skipped: {n, plural, one {# line is} other {# lines are}} longer than {max, number} characters and {n, plural, one {was} other {were}} not given to the secrets check (user names in paths were still checked).

summary.title: What happened
summary.cut: The traceback ends without an exception line.
summary.counts: {exceptions, plural, one {# exception} other {# exceptions}}, {frames, plural, one {# frame} other {# frames}}, {groups, plural, =0 {no exception group} one {# exception group} other {# exception groups}}.

look.title: Where to look first
look.caveat: A reading of the traceback, not a verdict: the frame where an exception is raised is not always where the mistake is. The bottom frame is the innermost call; CPython prints the outermost first (most recent call last).
look.raised-here: Exception {exc} ({type}) was raised in your code: {file}, line {line}, in {func}. Start there, with the values that reached that line.
look.raised-explicitly: Exception {exc} ({type}) was raised on purpose by a raise statement in {file}, line {line}, in {func}: the reason is in its message.
look.last-own-frame: Exception {exc} ({type}) was raised {inner}. The last frame of your own code before it is {file}, line {line}, in {func}: look there first, at what it passed in.
look.all-library: Exception {exc} ({type}) was raised {inner}, and no frame of your own code is shown: {file}, line {line}, in {func} is the innermost.
look.syntax: Exception {exc}: the file {file} did not compile, so none of it ran. Look at line {line}, column {column}, and just before it.
look.syntaxImported: Exception {exc}: the file {file} did not compile when {importFile}, line {importLine}, imported it. Look at line {line}, column {column} of {file}, and just before it.
look.no-traceback: Exception {exc} ({type}) has no traceback: it was created but never raised (a cause passed to raise ... from, or a member of a group), or only its last line was pasted.
look.recursion: Exception {exc} ({type}): the frame {file}, line {line}, in {func} repeats until the recursion limit. Look for the call that never stops.
look.interrupted: Exception {exc}: the program was stopped by Control-C (KeyboardInterrupt) while it was at {file}, line {line}, in {func}. That is where it was waiting, not a bug.
look.incomplete: Exception {exc}: its exception line is missing, so the paste looks cut. Paste the traceback down to its last line.
look.group-depth: Exception {exc}: CPython did not print this part of the group (past max_group_depth).

previous.cause: Its direct cause is exception {exc} ({type}), the original failure.
previous.context: It was raised while exception {exc} ({type}) was being handled, so the handler itself failed after that first failure.

release.title: Which release printed it
release.between: The format points to a release from 3.{min} to 3.{max}.
release.atLeast: The format points to Python 3.{v} or later.
release.atMost: The format points to Python 3.{v} or earlier.
release.unknown: Nothing in this traceback tells the release apart.
release.conflict: The evidence contradicts itself: the paste may mix output from two releases, or have been edited.
release.supported: Formats read: CPython 3.11 to 3.15, the releases supported on 27 October 2026 (3.10 reached end of life on 1 October 2026). Tested on 3.11.17, 3.12.3, 3.13.16 and 3.14.2; no 3.15 interpreter was available to test.

evidence.path-version: Line {line}: a path names the standard library of Python {detail}.
evidence.markers: Line {line}: ^ and ~ markers under a frame's source line: 3.11 or later (PEP 657).
evidence.call-markers: Line {line}: ~ under a called function with ^ under its parentheses: 3.13 or later.
evidence.multi-line: Line {line}: a frame shows an expression over several lines: 3.13 or later.
evidence.comprehension-frame: Line {line}: a frame for a comprehension ({detail}): 3.11 or earlier; 3.12 inlined comprehensions (PEP 709).
evidence.group: Line {line}: an exception group: 3.11 or later (PEP 654).
evidence.python-input: Line {line}: code typed into the interactive shell of 3.13 or later.
evidence.forgot-import: Line {line}: "Did you forget to import": 3.12 or later.
evidence.consider-renaming: Line {line}: "consider renaming" for a script that shadows a module: 3.13 or later.
evidence.suggestion-no-colon: Line {line}: a suggestion written "Did you mean '...'?" without a colon: 3.13 or later.
evidence.known-type: Line {line}: {detail} exists only in later releases.

sensitive.title: What may be sensitive
sensitive.none: Nothing that the checks look for was found. They are not complete: read the paste before you post it.
sensitive.warning: Before you post a traceback in an issue, a ticket or a chat, check it. Paths name users and hosts; source lines and messages can hold tokens and passwords; printed locals hold values. The redacted copy replaces user names with {user} and each finding with {redacted}; it does not find everything.

rules.home-directory: Line {line}: a user name in a home directory ({label}), {n, plural, one {once} other {# times}}.
rules.pem-private-key: Line {line}, column {column}: a private key block ({label}).
rules.aws-access-key-id: Line {line}, column {column}: an AWS access key ID.
rules.jwt: Line {line}, column {column}: a JSON Web Token ({label}).
rules.url-password: Line {line}, column {column}: a password in a URL ({label}).
rules.fortios-enc: Line {line}, column {column}: a FortiOS encrypted value ({label}).
rules.set-secret: Line {line}, column {column}: a secret set with set ({label}).
rules.keyword-value: Line {line}, column {column}: a password or passphrase attribute ({label}).
rules.json-member: Line {line}, column {column}: a secret-looking JSON member ({label}).
rules.yaml-mapping: Line {line}, column {column}: a secret-looking YAML key ({label}).
rules.shell-assignment: Line {line}, column {column}: a secret-looking shell variable ({label}).

chain.title: The exceptions, as printed
chain.single: One exception, with its frames from the outermost call to the innermost.
chain.order: {n, number} exceptions, oldest first: CPython prints the chain in the order it happened, and the last one is the exception the program stopped with.

link.cause: "The above exception was the direct cause of the following exception": the next exception was raised with raise ... from, on purpose, and the one above is its __cause__.
link.context: "During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred": the next exception was raised inside the handler of the one above, which became its __context__: the handler itself failed.

kinds.string: code run from a string (exec, compile or python -c)

inside.stdin: in code read from standard input
inside.string: in code run from a string

frame.noSource: No source line was printed: the file was not readable when the traceback was printed, or it is a frozen module.
frame.elided: {n, plural, one {# line} other {# lines}} of this expression {n, plural, one {is} other {are}} left out ({marker}).
frame.repeated: The same frame repeats {n, plural, one {# more time} other {# more times}}: CPython shows three and counts the rest.
frame.locals: {n, plural, one {# local variable} other {# local variables}} printed under this frame:

mark.expression: The markers point at the expression this frame was running: {text}
mark.call: ^ marks the call's parentheses {focus} and ~ the object called, {rest}: the exception came out of this call.
mark.subscript: ^ marks the subscript {focus} and ~ the object indexed, {rest}: the exception came out of this subscript.
mark.operator: ^ marks the operator {focus} and ~ its operands, {rest}: the exception came out of this operation.

exc.depthLimited: Exception {id}: a group nested past max_group_depth ({n, number}); CPython did not print it.
exc.noMessage: No message: the exception was raised without one (str() of it is empty).
exc.extra: {n, plural, one {One line follows} other {# lines follow}} the exception line: the rest of the message, or notes added with add_note() (PEP 678). The text alone cannot tell which.
exc.docs: Its entry in the Python documentation
exc.unknownModule: Not a class this tool knows. It is defined in the module {module}: read that module's documentation.
exc.unknownBare: Not a built-in this tool knows. CPython prints a class without its module only for built-ins and for classes of the script that was run (__main__), so it is most likely defined in that script.
exc.errno: The operating system's error number and text. The numbers differ between systems; the text is what the system calls it.
exc.gaiErrno: A negative number here is a getaddrinfo() result (one of socket's EAI_* constants), with the text gai_strerror() gives for it.
exc.codec: Codec {codec} could not handle {what} at position {position} (counted from 0): {reason}.
exc.framesOrder: {n, plural, one {One frame: where this exception was raised.} other {# frames, outermost first; the last is where this exception was raised.}}
exc.noTraceback: Printed without a traceback: this exception was never raised itself.

location.title: SyntaxError location
location.endOfLine: The marker points just past the end of the line: something is missing there (a colon, a bracket, a quote).

group.members: {n, plural, one {# member is} other {# members are}} shown{more, plural, =0 {} other {, # more are not}}. Each member keeps its own traceback, chain and notes.
group.more: "and {n, number} more": CPython prints 15 members of a group by default (max_group_width) and counts the rest.

suggestion.did-you-mean: CPython's own suggestion: did you mean {value}?
suggestion.forgot-import: CPython's own suggestion: the standard-library module {value} is used without being imported.
suggestion.shadows-stdlib: CPython's own diagnosis: the script {path} has the same name as the standard-library module {value}, so importing {value} imports the script. Rename the script.
suggestion.shadows-library: CPython's own diagnosis: the script {path} may have the same name as a library it imports. Rename the script.

excDesc.BaseException: The root of every exception class. Code is meant to derive from Exception, not from this.
excDesc.Exception: The base of every built-in exception that is not about leaving the program, and the base user-defined exceptions should derive from.
excDesc.ArithmeticError: The base of the arithmetic errors: OverflowError, ZeroDivisionError and FloatingPointError.
excDesc.AssertionError: An assert statement found its condition false.
excDesc.AttributeError: Reading or setting an attribute failed: the object has no attribute of that name.
excDesc.BaseExceptionGroup: A group of exceptions raised together, which may include ones that are not Exception subclasses (PEP 654).
excDesc.BlockingIOError: An operation would block on an object set to non-blocking mode, such as a socket (EAGAIN, EALREADY, EWOULDBLOCK, EINPROGRESS).
excDesc.BrokenPipeError: Writing to a pipe whose other end is closed, or to a socket shut down for writing (EPIPE, ESHUTDOWN).
excDesc.BufferError: A buffer-related operation could not be performed.
excDesc.BytesWarning: A warning about bytes and bytearray.
excDesc.ChildProcessError: An operation on a child process failed (ECHILD).
excDesc.ConnectionAbortedError: The peer aborted the connection attempt (ECONNABORTED).
excDesc.ConnectionError: The base of the connection errors: broken pipe, aborted, refused and reset.
excDesc.ConnectionRefusedError: The peer refused the connection attempt (ECONNREFUSED).
excDesc.DeprecationWarning: A warning, aimed at other Python developers, about a deprecated feature.
excDesc.EOFError: input() reached end of file without reading anything.
excDesc.EncodingWarning: A warning about encodings (the opt-in check for a missing encoding argument).
excDesc.ExceptionGroup: A group of Exception instances raised together (PEP 654), for example by asyncio.TaskGroup; except* handles its members by class.
excDesc.FileExistsError: Creating a file or directory that already exists (EEXIST).
excDesc.FileNotFoundError: A file or directory that was asked for does not exist (ENOENT).
excDesc.FutureWarning: A warning, aimed at the users of an application, about a deprecated feature.
excDesc.GeneratorExit: A generator or coroutine is being closed. It derives from BaseException because it is not an error.
excDesc.ImportError: An import statement could not load a module, or a name in from ... import was not found.
excDesc.ImportWarning: A warning about a probable mistake in module imports.
excDesc.IndentationError: A syntax error about wrong indentation.
excDesc.IndexError: A sequence index is out of range.
excDesc.InterruptedError: A system call was interrupted by a signal (EINTR).
excDesc.IsADirectoryError: A file operation was asked of a directory (EISDIR).
excDesc.KeyError: A mapping (a dictionary) has no such key. The message is the key's repr.
excDesc.KeyboardInterrupt: The user pressed the interrupt key, normally Control-C. It derives from BaseException so that except Exception does not catch it.
excDesc.LookupError: The base of the errors for an invalid key or index: IndexError and KeyError.
excDesc.MemoryError: An operation ran out of memory.
excDesc.ModuleNotFoundError: import could not locate the module.
excDesc.NameError: A name used in the code is not defined, locally or globally.
excDesc.NotADirectoryError: A directory operation was asked of something that is not a directory (ENOTDIR).
excDesc.NotImplementedError: A method that subclasses must override was called on a class that does not, or a feature is still to be written.
excDesc.OSError: A system function failed: file, socket and process errors, with the system's error number (errno) and text.
excDesc.OverflowError: An arithmetic result is too large to represent (integers grow instead; floats and some conversions overflow).
excDesc.PendingDeprecationWarning: A warning about a feature expected to be deprecated in the future.
excDesc.PermissionError: Not enough access rights, for example file permissions (EACCES, EPERM).
excDesc.PythonFinalizationError: An operation was blocked because the interpreter is shutting down.
excDesc.RecursionError: The interpreter's maximum recursion depth (sys.getrecursionlimit()) was exceeded.
excDesc.ReferenceError: A weak-reference proxy was used after its object was garbage-collected.
excDesc.ResourceWarning: A warning about resource use, such as a file or socket left open.
excDesc.RuntimeError: An error that fits no other category; the message says what went wrong.
excDesc.RuntimeWarning: A warning about dubious runtime behaviour.
excDesc.StopAsyncIteration: An asynchronous iterator has no more items.
excDesc.StopIteration: An iterator has no more items (next() or __next__).
excDesc.SyntaxError: The parser could not read the code: in a file being run or imported, or in compile(), exec() or eval().
excDesc.SyntaxWarning: A warning about dubious syntax, given while compiling.
excDesc.SystemError: An internal error of the interpreter; in CPython, often a C extension misusing the C API.
excDesc.SystemExit: sys.exit() was called. It derives from BaseException so that except Exception does not stop the exit.
excDesc.TabError: Indentation mixes tabs and spaces inconsistently.
excDesc.TimeoutError: A system function timed out (ETIMEDOUT); also what socket and asyncio timeouts raise (socket.timeout and asyncio.TimeoutError are aliases of it).
excDesc.TypeError: An operation or function got an object of the wrong type.
excDesc.UnboundLocalError: A local variable was read before any value was bound to it.
excDesc.UnicodeDecodeError: Bytes could not be decoded with the codec named in the message.
excDesc.UnicodeEncodeError: Text could not be encoded with the codec named in the message.
excDesc.UnicodeError: The base of the Unicode encoding and decoding errors; a ValueError.
excDesc.UserWarning: A warning issued by user code (the default category of warnings.warn()).
excDesc.ValueError: An argument had the right type but an unsuitable value.
excDesc.Warning: The base of the warning categories.
excDesc.ZeroDivisionError: The second operand of a division or modulo is zero.
excDesc.ImportCycleError: A lazy import failed because it imports itself, directly or not (3.15).
excDesc.socket_gaierror: An address error from getaddrinfo() or getnameinfo(): the name or address could not be resolved or was not valid. The number is one of the EAI_* constants.
excDesc.socket_herror: An address error from the older h_errno functions, such as gethostbyname_ex() and gethostbyaddr().
excDesc.ssl_SSLError: An error from the TLS implementation (OpenSSL); the code and message come from the library.
excDesc.ssl_SSLZeroReturnError: The TLS connection was closed cleanly; the TCP connection may still be open.
excDesc.ssl_SSLWantReadError: A non-blocking TLS socket needs more data from the network before it can go on.
excDesc.ssl_SSLWantWriteError: A non-blocking TLS socket needs to send more data before it can go on.
excDesc.ssl_SSLSyscallError: A system error on a TLS socket; the original errno is not available.
excDesc.ssl_SSLEOFError: The TLS connection was ended abruptly; do not reuse the transport.
excDesc.ssl_SSLCertVerificationError: Certificate validation failed; verify_code and verify_message say why.
excDesc.json_decoder_JSONDecodeError: The text is not valid JSON; the message gives the line, column and character position where decoding stopped.
excDesc.asyncio_exceptions_CancelledError: An asyncio operation was cancelled. A BaseException since 3.8; code that catches it should almost always raise it again.
excDesc.asyncio_exceptions_InvalidStateError: A Task or Future was in the wrong state, for example given a result twice.
excDesc.asyncio_exceptions_IncompleteReadError: An asyncio stream read did not get all the bytes it asked for before the end of the stream.
excDesc.asyncio_exceptions_LimitOverrunError: An asyncio stream reached its buffer limit while looking for a separator.
excDesc.subprocess_SubprocessError: The base of the subprocess module's exceptions.
excDesc.subprocess_CalledProcessError: A command run with check=True (or check_call, check_output) exited with a non-zero status.
excDesc.subprocess_TimeoutExpired: A child process did not finish within its timeout.
excDesc.urllib_error_URLError: urllib could not open the URL; reason says why (often an OSError, such as a refused connection or a failed name lookup).
excDesc.urllib_error_HTTPError: The server answered with an HTTP error status; code, reason and headers hold the response.
excDesc.urllib_error_ContentTooShortError: urlretrieve() got less data than the Content-Length header announced.
excDesc.http_client_RemoteDisconnected: The server closed the connection without sending a response.
excDesc.http_client_IncompleteRead: A subclass of HTTPException; the documentation gives no further detail.
excDesc.http_client_BadStatusLine: The server answered with a status line http.client does not understand.
excDesc.http_client_InvalidURL: A port was given that is not numeric, or is empty.
excDesc.http_client_LineTooLong: The server sent an excessively long line.

hint.none-value: The object is None where something else was expected. A function without a return statement returns None, and re.match() and re.search() return None when nothing matches: check what produced the value.
hint.ModuleNotFoundError: Check that the module is installed in the environment that ran the script (a virtual environment only sees what was installed in it) and that its name is spelt as it is installed.
hint.ImportError: The module was found, but loading it or finding the name in from ... import failed; check the name and, for a circular import, the order the modules import each other.
hint.NameError: Check the spelling, that the name is defined before this line runs, and that a module is imported.
hint.UnboundLocalError: An assignment to this name somewhere in the function makes it local everywhere in it; it is read before that assignment runs.
hint.AttributeError: Check the object's type at that line: the attribute may be misspelt, or the object is not what the code expects.
hint.KeyError: The key in the message is not in the dictionary. dict.get(key, default) returns a default instead of raising.
hint.IndexError: Compare the length of the sequence with the index at that line.
hint.TypeError: Check the types of the values at that line: a value of one type where another was expected, or a call with the wrong arguments.
hint.ValueError: The type was right but the value was not: check the value the message quotes and where it came from.
hint.ZeroDivisionError: Check where the divisor comes from: an empty interval or a zero count.
hint.RecursionError: A function calls itself (directly or through others) without reaching a stopping case; the repeated frame shows which.
hint.AssertionError: An assert found its condition false. Note that python -O removes assert statements, so they are no substitute for checks.
hint.KeyboardInterrupt: Someone pressed Control-C; the frames show where the program was at that moment.
hint.FileNotFoundError: Check the path in the message, and the current directory the script ran from when the path is relative.
hint.PermissionError: The account running the script lacks the access rights the operation needs.
hint.ConnectionRefusedError: The peer refused the connection (ECONNREFUSED): check the address and port, and that the service listens there.
hint.ConnectionResetError: The peer reset the connection (ECONNRESET) while it was in use: the other side's logs usually say why.
hint.BrokenPipeError: The other end had already closed when the program wrote.
hint.TimeoutError: Nothing answered in time: check the address and port, the path to the device, and the timeout the code set.
hint.UnicodeDecodeError: The bytes are not in the codec used to decode them: find out the real encoding, or choose an error handler (replace, backslashreplace, surrogateescape) on purpose.
hint.UnicodeEncodeError: The text has a character the target codec cannot represent: use a codec that can (UTF-8), or choose an error handler on purpose.
hint.SyntaxError: The file did not compile, so nothing in it ran. The markers show where the parser detected the error, which, as the tutorial says, is not always the place that needs to be fixed: look just before it too.
hint.IndentationError: Check the indentation of the marked line against the block it belongs to.
hint.TabError: Use spaces only (or tabs only) for indentation in the file.
hint.socket_gaierror: The name did not resolve, or the address is not valid: check the spelling, DNS, and whether it is a literal address with a typo.
hint.json_decoder_JSONDecodeError: The text was not JSON; the message says where decoding stopped (line 1 column 1, char 0, is the very first character, as with an empty text). Print what was decoded before decoding it.
hint.ssl_SSLCertVerificationError: The certificate did not validate; verify_message says why (an untrusted issuer, an expired certificate, a host name that does not match). Turning verification off (CERT_NONE) accepts just about any certificate, so fix the cause instead.
hint.subprocess_CalledProcessError: The command ran and failed: its exit status and command line are in the message; capture its stderr to see why.
hint.subprocess_TimeoutExpired: The child process ran past its timeout and was not waited for further.
hint.asyncio_exceptions_CancelledError: A task was cancelled, often by a timeout or by a TaskGroup after another task failed: look for the other error.
hint.http_client_RemoteDisconnected: The server closed the connection without sending any response: check that the scheme and port of the URL match what the server speaks.
hint.urllib_error_URLError: The reason in the message is the real error, usually an OSError such as a refused connection or a name that did not resolve.
hint.urllib_error_HTTPError: The server answered with an HTTP error: the status code says which, and the body of the response often says why.
hint.ExceptionGroup: Several errors travel together here: read each member on its own; the first leaf is not necessarily the most important.
hint.BaseExceptionGroup: Several errors travel together, at least one of them not an Exception (KeyboardInterrupt or CancelledError, for example): read each member.

share.carries: The link carries the redacted copy ({user}, {redacted}), never the traceback as pasted.
share.blocked: No link: {n, plural, one {one line is} other {# lines are}} longer than {max, number} characters and went unchecked for secrets.

wheel-filename-explainer.name: Wheel filename & PEP 440 version explainer
wheel-filename-explainer.blurb: Take a wheel or sdist file name apart: name, version, build tag and every compatibility tag, which Pythons and systems it installs on, and whether it fits a given interpreter. Also normalizes, sorts and matches PEP 440 versions.
wheel-filename-explainer.fileLabel: Wheel or sdist file name (or a URL to one)
wheel-filename-explainer.runsLocally: Read in your browser: nothing is sent or downloaded, and a URL is only cut down to its file name.
wheel-filename-explainer.tooLong: The input is longer than {max, number} characters, so it was not read.

verdict.wheel: A valid wheel file name: {name} version {version}.
verdict.sdist: A valid source distribution file name: {name} version {version}.
verdict.sdistZip: A source distribution file name in the older .zip form: {name} version {version}.
verdict.invalid: Not a valid wheel or source distribution file name. The findings say why.
verdict.unknown: Not a wheel or source distribution file name.

wheel-filename-explainer.fromPath: Read from a URL or a path: the file name is {name}.

meaning.name: The project name. Normalized for comparison: {normalized}. A wheel or sdist file name writes it as {escaped}.
meaning.build: A build number: sorts by {number} first, then by the text {rest}. It only breaks a tie between wheels that are identical in everything else; it is not part of the version.
meaning.buildNumber: A build number ({number}). It only breaks a tie between wheels that are identical in everything else; it is not part of the version.
meaning.pythonMajor: {impl} {major}, any minor version: a major-only tag is not shorthand for {major}.0; it means the packager released a wheel meant to work across {major}.x versions.
meaning.pythonGeneric: Any Python implementation, version {version} (py means the code needs no implementation-specific feature).
meaning.pythonGenericMajor: Any Python implementation, any {major}.x: a major-only tag is not shorthand for {major}.0; it means the packager released a wheel meant to work across {major}.x versions.
meaning.pythonOther: The implementation {impl} (one without a two-letter code), version {version}.
meaning.pythonUnreadable: Not a python tag the explainer can read: letters, then a version such as 3 or 313.

abi.none: No ABI requirement: the wheel has no extension module tied to a Python ABI.
abi.abi3: The CPython stable ABI: compiled once against the Limited API and loaded by later CPython versions that are not free-threaded.
abi.abi3t: The stable ABI for free-threaded CPython (PEP 803, from Python 3.15).
abi.pypy: The ABI of PyPy for Python {version}, PyPy release pp{release} (pp73 is PyPy 7.3).

abiFlag.u: Flag u: wide Unicode (Python 3.2 and older).
abiFlag.x: Flag {flag}: not one the explainer knows.

platform.manylinux: Linux with glibc {major}.{minor} or newer on {arch}.
platform.manylinuxLegacy: Linux with glibc {major}.{minor} or newer on {arch}; {legacy} is the older name of manylinux_{major}_{minor}.
platform.musllinux: Linux with musl {major}.{minor} or newer on {arch}, for example Alpine Linux (packaging, and so pip, lists only the same major version of musl).
platform.linux: Linux on {arch}, with no statement about the C library: the simple form, which the specification calls insufficient for public distribution.
platform.macosMulti: macOS {major}.{minor} or later, one binary for {archs} ({arch}).
platform.ios: iOS {major}.{minor} or later on {arch}, built with the {sdk} SDK (software development kit).
platform.android: Android API level {api} or later, ABI {abi}.
platform.pyemscripten: Emscripten (WebAssembly, for example Pyodide in a browser), platform {year}_{patch}.
platform.other: Another platform: {tag} is the value of sysconfig.get_platform() on that system, with - and . written as _.

wheel-filename-explainer.compressedNote: A tag written with dots (py2.py3, for example) is a compressed set: the wheel stands for every combination of its python, ABI and platform tags.
wheel-filename-explainer.installsTitle: What each tag combination needs ({n, plural, one {# combination} other {# combinations}})
wheel-filename-explainer.installsNote: An installer keeps an ordered list of the tags its interpreter and system accept, and installs a wheel when one of the wheel's tags is in that list. The interpreter column follows the list packaging 26.3 builds.

rule.anyFrom: Any Python implementation, version {major}.{minor} or a later {major}.x.
rule.pypyMajor: Any PyPy for Python {major} (pip lists pp{major}-none-any for PyPy).
rule.cpythonAbi: CPython {version} only, a build that is not free-threaded.
rule.flagUcs4: Built with wide Unicode (Python 3.2 and older).
rule.stableAbi3: CPython {version} or later, builds that are not free-threaded (stable ABI).
rule.stableAbi3t: CPython {version} or later, free-threaded builds only: pip lists abi3t only for those, and abi3.abi3t covers both kinds of build.
rule.pypyAbi: PyPy for Python {version}, PyPy ABI pp{release}.
rule.implAbi: The implementation {impl}, with its own ABI {abi}.

impossible.stable-abi-not-cpython: No installer lists it: abi3 and abi3t are CPython's stable ABIs and need a cp python tag.
impossible.generic-with-abi: No installer lists it: a generic py tag never comes with an ABI other than none.
impossible.abi-version-mismatch: No installer lists it: the ABI names a different Python version from the python tag.
impossible.major-only-with-abi: No installer lists it: pip lists CPython tags with a minor version, such as cp313, never a major-only cp3 tag.
impossible.abi-with-any-platform: No installer lists it: a wheel with a compiled ABI is built for a platform, never for any.
impossible.pypy-major-with-platform: No installer lists it: pip lists pp3 only with the platform any.
impossible.pypy-version-any: No installer lists it: PyPy lists a pp tag with a version together with a platform, and pp3-none-any for pure Python.
impossible.unreadable: The python tag cannot be read, so nothing can be said about it.

finding.not-a-distribution: The name does not end in .whl (a wheel), .tar.gz (a source distribution) or .zip (an older source distribution).
finding.suffix-case: The suffix must be written in lower case: tools compare it exactly (.whl, .tar.gz).
finding.wrong-part-count: A wheel file name has 4 or 5 hyphens (name, version, an optional build tag, then three tags); this one has {hyphens}.
finding.sdist-no-hyphen: A source distribution file name needs a hyphen between the name and the version.
finding.empty-name: Nothing comes before the first hyphen, so there is no project name.
finding.double-underscore: The name part contains a double underscore: a wheel writes every run of -, _ and . as a single _, so pip refuses it.
finding.bad-name: Not a valid project name: only ASCII letters, digits, ., _ and -, starting and ending with a letter or a digit (the problem is at character {at}).
finding.bad-version: The version part is not a PEP 440 version.
finding.bad-build-tag: A build tag must start with a digit.
finding.empty-tag: A tag, or a member of a compressed tag set, is empty (two dots in a row, or a dot at either end).
finding.python-tag-not-identifier: The python tag {tag} is not an identifier (it must not start with a digit), so pip refuses the name.
finding.name-not-escaped: Accepted, but not how a tool writes it today: lower case, with every run of -, _ and . as a single _ ({expected}).
finding.version-not-normalized: The version is not in its normal form ({normalized}); tools write normalized versions in file names.
finding.local-version: The version has a local label (after +): fine for private builds, but PyPI does not allow local versions.
finding.build-tag-used: A build tag is present. It is not part of the version, so a fix that people must be able to refer to from outside (in a security advisory, for example) should get a new version instead.
finding.tags-not-sorted: The compressed set {set} is not sorted; the specification writes its members sorted.
finding.tags-uppercase: A tag has upper-case letters; tags are compared in lower case.
finding.unknown-python-tag: The python tag {tag} is not letters followed by a version.
finding.unknown-platform: {tag} is not one of the platform families the specification describes; it is read as another system's sysconfig platform.
finding.linux-simple-tag: {tag} is the simple Linux form, which the specification calls insufficient for public distribution; manylinux and musllinux tags state which C library the wheel needs.
finding.legacy-manylinux: {tag} is a legacy name: it means {alias} (PEP 600).
finding.legacy-arch-mismatch: {legacy} was not defined for this architecture ({tag}).
finding.macos-version-shape: {tag}: macOS tags use 10_y for macOS 10 and x_0 from macOS 11 on, with x from 10 to 15 or 26 and later.
finding.android-abi: {tag}: Android tags use one of four ABIs (armeabi_v7a, arm64_v8a, x86, x86_64).
finding.ios-multiarch: {tag}: iOS tags use arm64_iphoneos, arm64_iphonesimulator or x86_64_iphonesimulator.
finding.sdist-zip: The standard source distribution is a .tar.gz; .zip is the older form.
finding.sdist-hyphens: The file name has more than one hyphen: the name is read as everything before the last one, as pip does, but a standard sdist file name has exactly one.
finding.too-many-tags: The tag sets expand to {count, number} combinations; the first {max, number} are explained.

versionError.expected-number: A version starts with a number (character {at}).
versionError.bad-local: The local label after + must be letters and digits separated by single dots, hyphens or underscores (character {at}).
versionError.unexpected: Nothing in the version scheme accepts what is at character {at}.

target.title: Does it install on this interpreter and system?
target.yes: Installs: the best match is {tag}, number {rank, number} in this interpreter's list of {total, number} accepted tags.
target.no: Does not install: none of the wheel's tags is among the {total, number} tags this interpreter accepts.
target.howNote: The list is the one packaging 26.3 builds for the interpreter and system described. pip 26.2 still vendors packaging 26.2, which puts the plain linux_ tag after the manylinux and musllinux tags of each group instead of before them, so the list python -m pip debug --verbose prints holds the same tags, and only the plain linux_ tag of each group moves.
target.pypyNote: A PyPy target is taken to be PyPy 7.3 (ABI pp{release}).

wheel-filename-explainer.versionsLabel: Versions (separated by spaces, commas or new lines)

versions.title: {n, plural, one {# version} other {# versions}}
versions.localOnly: Already in normal form; a version with a local label is never the canonical public form.
versions.orderNote: Numbers compare as numbers and a missing release number counts as zero. Within one release, .dev comes first, then a, b and rc, then the release itself, then .post; a version with a local label sorts after the same version without one.
versions.truncated: Only the first {max, number} versions were read.

note.whitespace: White space around it was dropped.
note.zeros: Leading zeros were dropped from a number.
note.pre-separator: The separator before or inside the pre-release was dropped.
note.pre-spelling: alpha, beta, c, pre or preview was written as a, b or rc.
note.pre-implicit: The pre-release had no number, so 0 was added.
note.post-separator: The post-release was written with a single dot (.post).
note.post-spelling: rev or r was written as post.
note.post-implicit-number: The post-release had no number, so 0 was added.
note.post-implicit: A hyphen and a number after the release were read as a post-release.
note.dev-separator: The development release was written with a single dot (.dev).
note.dev-implicit: The development release had no number, so 0 was added.
note.local-separator: Hyphens and underscores in the local label were written as dots.
note.epoch-zero: The epoch 0! was dropped (0 is the default).

spec.title: The specifier set
spec.empty: An empty set: every version matches.

policy.named: A clause names a pre-release, so pre-releases in range are taken too.
policy.only-prereleases: Only pre-releases are in range, so they are taken: an installer may warn that a pre-release was needed.
policy.excluded: Pre-releases (development releases included) are left out because a final or post-release is in range, unless pre-releases are explicitly requested.

clause.arbitrary: the text {v} exactly (letters compared without regard to case); heavily discouraged
clause.prefix: any version whose release starts with {prefix}
clause.notPrefix: any version whose release does not start with {prefix}
clause.equal: exactly {v} (a missing release number counts as zero; a candidate's local label is ignored)
clause.notEqualLocal: anything but {v} with that local label
clause.lt: earlier than {v}, without the pre-releases of {v} unless {v} is itself one
clause.gt: later than {v}, without the post-releases and local versions of {v} unless {v} is itself a post-release

specError.empty: an empty clause (two commas, or a comma with nothing before it)
specError.no-operator: does not start with one of ~=, ==, !=, <=, >=, <, > or ===
specError.bad-version: the version is not a PEP 440 version
specError.bad-characters: contains a character a version cannot contain (two clauses need a comma between them)
specError.local-not-allowed: a local label (after +) is only allowed with == and !=
specError.wildcard-after-suffix: .* may only follow release numbers (pip refuses 1.0a1.* and the like)
specError.compatible-one-segment: ~= needs at least two release numbers (~=1 is not allowed)

share.carries: {mode, select, versions {The link carries the versions and the specifier set as typed.} other {The link carries the file name as typed, with the target when the check is open; a URL with credentials gets none.}}
share.blockedCredentials: No link: the URL holds credentials before its @ (a password, or a token in the user name's place). Paste the file name alone, then share again.

pyproject-toml-explainer.name: pyproject.toml explainer
pyproject-toml-explainer.blurb: Paste a pyproject.toml and read it table by table and key by key: what each key is for, the core metadata field it fills, every dependency taken apart, and the rules of the packaging specifications it breaks, each marked error, warning or note.
pyproject-toml-explainer.runsLocally: Read in your browser by the site's own TOML parser: nothing is sent, nothing is installed, and no URL or file named in it is opened.
pyproject-toml-explainer.tooLong: The file is longer than {max, number} characters, so it was not read.

sum.name: Name: {name}
sum.versionDynamic: Version: dynamic (the build back-end provides it)
sum.counts: {error, plural, one {# error} other {# errors}}, {warning, plural, one {# warning} other {# warnings}}, {note, plural, one {# note} other {# notes}}

pyproject-toml-explainer.severityNote: Error: the specification says MUST or MUST NOT, or the value has the wrong type. Warning: SHOULD or SHOULD NOT, something a tool MAY refuse, or something deprecated. Note: worth knowing, nothing to fix.
pyproject-toml-explainer.clean: Nothing to report: the file follows every rule the explainer checks.

section.other: A table the specification does not define

absent.build-system: is absent: build front-ends use requires = ["setuptools"] and the legacy setuptools build
absent.project: is absent: the build back-end supplies all the metadata itself

bs.requires: The packages the build front-end installs before it builds (dependency specifiers). Mandatory in the table.
bs.build-backend: The build back-end: the module, and optionally the object, that the front-end imports and calls to build the sdist and the wheel.
bs.backend-path: Directories, relative to the project root, put at the start of sys.path to load a back-end kept in the source tree. They must stay inside the source tree.

p.name: The project's name, the one key every [project] table must give statically.
p.version: The version, a PEP 440 version. Given here or listed in dynamic.
p.description: A one-line summary of the project.
p.readme: The long description: a file path (its suffix gives the content type) or a table with file or text and content-type.
p.requires-python: The Python versions the project is compatible with, as a version specifier set; installers may look at it when picking which release to install.
p.license: The licence as an SPDX licence expression (the old table form is deprecated).
p.license-files: Glob patterns for the licence files to ship in the distributions, relative to the directory holding pyproject.toml.
p.authors: The people or organizations who wrote the project: tables with name, email or both.
p.maintainers: The people or organizations who maintain the project: tables with name, email or both.
p.classifiers: Trove classifiers that apply to the project.
p.urls: Labelled links (home page, source, documentation and so on); the label is normalized before it is compared with the well-known labels.
p.scripts: Commands to install: each key is the command name and each value an object reference (the console_scripts entry point group).
p.gui-scripts: Commands to install for graphical programs (the gui_scripts entry point group): on Windows they are wrapped in a GUI executable and can start without a console.
p.entry-points: Other entry point groups, one sub-table per group, for plugins other software discovers.
p.dependencies: What the project needs at run time, one dependency specifier per string; always considered when it is installed.
p.optional-dependencies: Extras: named lists of dependencies installed only when asked for, as in name[extra].
p.import-names: The import names the project provides (PEP 794); an import name may end in ; private.
p.import-namespaces: Import names the project provides but not exclusively, as with namespace packages several projects contribute to (PEP 794).
p.dynamic: The keys the build back-end fills in at build time instead of this file.

dg.group: A dependency group named {name}: requirements and includes of other groups, for development tasks. Back-ends never write it into the metadata of built distributions.

tool.table: Settings for the tool {name}. The sub-table tool.{name} belongs to the project that owns the name {name} on PyPI.

key.other: Not a key the specification defines here: {name}.

detail.readmeText: The text given in the table, content type {type}.
detail.url: {label} (normalised {normalized}): not one of the well-known labels.
detail.entryInvalid: not an object reference (module or module:object)
detail.backendObject: The front-end imports {module} and uses its attribute {object}.
detail.backendModule: The front-end imports {module} and uses the module itself.

field.python_version: python_version: the first two parts of the Python version, such as 3.13
field.python_full_version: python_full_version: the whole Python version, such as 3.13.16
field.os_name: os_name: os.name, such as posix or nt
field.sys_platform: sys_platform: sys.platform, such as linux, darwin or win32
field.platform_release: platform_release: platform.release(), the operating system release
field.platform_system: platform_system: platform.system(), such as Linux, Darwin or Windows
field.platform_version: platform_version: platform.version(), the operating system version
field.platform_machine: platform_machine: platform.machine(), such as x86_64 or arm64
field.platform_python_implementation: platform_python_implementation: such as CPython or PyPy
field.extra: extra: the extra being installed (only meaningful inside a distribution's metadata)
field.extras: extras: the extras requested (lock files only)
field.dependency_groups: dependency_groups: the dependency groups requested (lock files only)

fieldType.version-or-string: compared as a version when both sides are valid versions, otherwise as a string

marker.legacy-field: {written} is an old spelling of {field}; it is not in the grammar, though packaging still reads it
marker.no-field: both sides are constants, so the comparison never depends on the environment; tools may refuse it
marker.string-ordered: {field} is a string field, and ordered comparisons ({op}) on strings should be reported as errors
marker.string-version-op: {op} is a version operator; on the string field {field} it should be reported as an error
marker.version-in: in and not in are not valid on the version field {field}
marker.version-bad-constant: {value} is not a valid version, so it cannot be compared with the version field {field}
marker.set-misuse: {field} is a set: it is only tested as "value" in {field} or "value" not in {field}
marker.lock-file-field: {field} is only defined in lock files, not in a project's own dependencies
marker.extra-other-op: extra is only compared with ==; {op} has no defined meaning for it
marker.extra-not-normalized: the extra is compared after name normalization, as {normalized}
marker.string-characters: the string {value} has characters outside the ones the grammar lists; tools may accept them

reqError.expected-name: a dependency specifier starts with a project name
reqError.bad-extras: the extras must be names separated by commas inside [ ]
reqError.bad-specifier: a version clause is not valid
reqError.expected-url: @ must be followed by a URL
reqError.expected-marker: ; must be followed by an environment marker
reqError.bad-marker: the environment marker does not follow the grammar
reqError.unterminated-string: a quoted string in the marker is not closed
reqError.too-deep: the marker's parentheses are nested too deeply (more than 64 levels)
reqError.trailing: something follows the end of the dependency specifier

versionError.expected-number: a version starts with a number
versionError.bad-local: the local label after + must be letters and digits separated by single dots, hyphens or underscores
versionError.unexpected: nothing in the version scheme accepts what follows

licenseError.unknown-license: {token} is not on the SPDX License List 3.29.0
licenseError.unknown-exception: {token} is not on the SPDX exceptions list 3.29.0
licenseError.bad-license-ref: {token} is not a valid LicenseRef- (the prefix is written LicenseRef-, followed by letters, digits, dots or hyphens)
licenseError.unsupported-ref: {token}: the packaging specification accepts SPDX identifiers and LicenseRef- only
licenseError.operator-case: {token}: operators are written all in upper case or all in lower case
licenseError.syntax: an operator, an operand or a parenthesis is out of place at {token}
licenseError.too-deep: the parentheses are nested more than 64 levels deep

globProblem.parent: a pattern must not use .. to leave the project directory
globProblem.absolute: a pattern must be relative, never an absolute path
globProblem.characters: only letters, digits, underscores, hyphens, dots, slashes, spaces, * ? and [ ] are allowed
globProblem.bracket: a [ ] range is not closed or not opened

nameProblem.bad-character: only ASCII letters, digits, dots, underscores and hyphens are allowed
nameProblem.bad-start: the name must start with a letter or a digit
nameProblem.bad-end: the name must end with a letter or a digit

urlIssue.insecure: the URL does not use a secure transport (https, or ssh for version control)
urlIssue.no-hash: the URL carries no hash (a hash fragment, or a commit hash for version control)
urlIssue.insecure-no-hash: the URL uses no secure transport and carries no hash

specError.empty: an empty clause (two commas, or a comma with nothing before it)
specError.no-operator: a clause does not start with one of ~=, ==, !=, <=, >=, <, > or ===
specError.bad-version: the version is not a PEP 440 version
specError.bad-characters: a character a version cannot contain (two clauses need a comma between them)
specError.local-not-allowed: a local label (after +) is only allowed with == and !=
specError.compatible-one-segment: ~= needs at least two release numbers

clause.prefix: any version whose release starts with {prefix}
clause.notPrefix: any version whose release does not start with {prefix}
clause.lt: earlier than {v}, without the pre-releases of {v} unless {v} is itself one
clause.gt: later than {v}, without the post-releases of {v} unless {v} is itself a post-release
